author: reubenob
body:
This pull request introduces support for pausing and resuming robot actions based on uncertainty signals, improves camera selection for RND training, and updates configuration files for robot and teleop device ports and camera streams. The main changes are grouped below.

### Uncertainty-based pause/resume support

* Added an uncertainty pause mechanism to `LeRobotROS2Bridge`, including a subscriber to `/uncertainty/pause`, state tracking, and callbacks for pause/resume events. This allows the robot to stop actions when uncertainty is high and resume when normalized. (`src/lerobot/common/robot_devices/ros2_bridge.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bfc128eea48f1a34a7ea2de5891c4bf5f87622a46be4401129953517eea7589eL31-R32) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bfc128eea48f1a34a7ea2de5891c4bf5f87622a46be4401129953517eea7589eR65-R69) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bfc128eea48f1a34a7ea2de5891c4bf5f87622a46be4401129953517eea7589eR127-R136) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-bfc128eea48f1a34a7ea2de5891c4bf5f87622a46be4401129953517eea7589eR164-R215)
* Updated `so101_follower` robot's `send_action` method to skip sending actions when paused due to high uncertainty, returning the input action unchanged. (`src/lerobot/robots/so101_follower/so101_follower.py`)
* In the recording loop, reset the policy when resuming from an uncertainty pause to ensure proper action queue handling. (`src/lerobot/record.py`)

### Camera stream and configuration updates

* Added support for the `aria` camera stream (ROS2 topic `/aria/eye_gaze/visualization_small`) in both `record.yaml` and `record_eval.yaml`, and updated robot and teleop device ports. Also changed `display_data` defaults to `false` and adjusted episode timing. (`launch/record.yaml`, `launch/record_eval.yaml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dcdbb75b0bfd39aa90549840a17782432bb7361a19f9e603c1a297e9f69cd336L3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dcdbb75b0bfd39aa90549840a17782432bb7361a19f9e603c1a297e9f69cd336R32-R49) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-777c3387742894ee1b5e6b3438a515214f889154af1518acd018aebaa2f63161L3-R3) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-777c3387742894ee1b5e6b3438a515214f889154af1518acd018aebaa2f63161R34-R51)

### RND training improvements

* Enhanced RND training script to allow selection of a specific camera key, with command-line arguments and error handling for unavailable cameras. The camera key and available cameras are now logged and saved in training metadata. (`src/lerobot/scripts/train_rnd.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bac077670a1252a90d26ca0c310a42f30de1f13d4b31390874c5132eee6da487L127-R151) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bac077670a1252a90d26ca0c310a42f30de1f13d4b31390874c5132eee6da487R404-R409) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bac077670a1252a90d26ca0c310a42f30de1f13d4b31390874c5132eee6da487R423) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-bac077670a1252a90d26ca0c310a42f30de1f13d4b31390874c5132eee6da487R329-R339)
* Increased the rolling window size for uncertainty estimation in the RND module from 10 to 50 for improved stability. (`src/lerobot/common/uncertainty/rnd_module.py`)

### Minor improvements

* Added usage documentation for training RND with a specific camera stream. (`src/lerobot/scripts/train_rnd.py`)
* Updated function signatures and docstrings in the RND training script for clarity and expanded argument support. (`src/lerobot/scripts/train_rnd.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bac077670a1252a90d26ca0c310a42f30de1f13d4b31390874c5132eee6da487L78-R92) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bac077670a1252a90d26ca0c310a42f30de1f13d4b31390874c5132eee6da487R196-R212)

body: ## Summary This PR contains the code of the migration from LNbits UserManager extension to LNbits v1+ core Users API, fixing user identification and wallet balance display issues across the application. It also included the Branding color code updates. ## Problem After the initial Users API migration, several issues remained: 1. Transaction feed showing "Unknown" for user names 2. Total Zaps Component stuck on "Loading..." 3. Wallet page showing "0 coins" for both Private and Allowance wallets 4. TypeScript compilation errors with null safety **Root Cause**: The application was attempting to match users by `aadObjectId` in the `extra` metadata field, but LNbits stores the Azure AD Object ID in the `external_id` field (a top-level field on the user object). ## Testing - Feed displays correct user names - Total Zaps statistics update correctly - Private wallet balance displays correctly - Allowance wallet balance displays correctly - TypeScript compiles without errors - No console errors during normal operation ##Screenshots ## Migration Notes This PR assumes that: 1. Azure AD Object IDs are stored in LNbits users' external_id field 2. Users have wallets named "Private" and "Allowance" (case-insensitive search) 3. Wallet balances are stored as balance_msat and need to be converted to sats ## Related Issues Closes #108 (or your issue number) Closes #119 Closes #28 This PR summary covers all the work we did and explains the root cause, the fix, and the technical details. author: benwolst
body:
## Summary

Fixes the R-CMD-check workflow so that odiff is actually available during tests.

**Problem**: Previously, tests were being silently skipped on ALL platforms because `npm install -g odiff-bin` doesn't automatically add the npm global bin directory to PATH. This meant:
- Ubuntu: 42+ tests skipped
- Windows: 99+ tests skipped
- macOS: tests skipped

The tests "passed" only because `skip_if_no_odiff()` gracefully skipped them, then `odiffr_update()` fallback downloaded from GitHub releases.

**Fix**:
- Add npm bin directory to `GITHUB_PATH` on all platforms
- Add symlink fallback for Unix when odiff binary doesn't exist (matches test-coverage.yaml)
- Add `npm rebuild` workaround for Windows cmd-shim bug (where `odiff.cmd` incorrectly runs `.exe` through `node`)
- Add verification step to confirm odiff is accessible before R check

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml`: Split "Install odiff" into Unix and Windows steps with proper PATH setup

## Test Plan

- [x] CI passes on all platforms with tests actually running via npm-installed odiff
- [x] "Verify odiff installation" step shows version output
- [x] Test count should increase (not skipped)

body:
Implement manual camera activation/deactivation controls for the barcode scanner to improve performance and user experience.

## Problem
- Camera auto-initialized on every render causing performance issues
- No user control over camera activation
- Wasted device resources when not actively scanning
- Error handling triggered repeatedly on each render

## Solution
Implemented manual camera toggle system with activation button:
- Camera only starts when user explicitly clicks "Activar Cámara"
- Camera automatically stops after successful scan (500ms delay)
- Manual "Detener Cámara" button for user control
- Proper camera lifecycle management

## Changes

### BarcodeScanner Component (src/app/pos/components/BarcodeScanner.tsx)
- Added isActive state to track camera status
- Added new props: onActivate, autoHideOnScan (default: true)
- Implemented handleActivate() with focus management
- Implemented handleDeactivate() to stop camera
- Modified handleScanSuccess() with auto-hide behavior
- Enhanced handleError() to only process errors when active
- Added inactive state UI with purple gradient "Activar Cámara" button
- Added active state UI with "Detener Cámara" button
- Imported Camera and StopCircle icons from lucide-react
- Improved accessibility with ARIA labels and focus management

### ScanditBarcodeScanner Component (src/components/barcode/ScanditBarcodeScanner.tsx)
- Added isActive prop to control scanner lifecycle
- Modified initialization to only run when isActive is true
- Updated camera state management to respond to isActive changes
- Added isActive to useEffect dependency arrays
- Prevents initialization and errors when inactive

## Benefits
- ✅ Camera does NOT auto-initialize on page load
- ✅ Reduced battery usage and device resource consumption
- ✅ No repeated initialization on re-renders
- ✅ Better error handling (errors only during active scanning)
- ✅ User control over camera activation
- ✅ Auto-cleanup after successful scans

## UI/UX Improvements
- Clear visual feedback for inactive vs active states
- Purple gradient styling matching app theme
- Touch targets ≥44px for mobile accessibility
- Focus management for keyboard navigation
- Responsive design (mobile-first)

## Testing
- ✅ Build successful with no TypeScript errors
- ✅ Camera lifecycle properly managed
- ✅ Auto-hide after scan works correctly
- ✅ Manual stop button functions properly

author: jumski
body:
# Add Advisory Locks to Prevent Concurrent Flow Compilation Race Conditions

This PR adds transaction-level advisory locks to the `ensure_flow_compiled` function to prevent race conditions during concurrent flow compilation attempts. The implementation:

- Generates a deterministic lock key from the flow slug using `hashtext()`
- Acquires a transaction-level advisory lock with `pg_advisory_xact_lock(1, v_lock_key)`
- Ensures that concurrent compilation attempts for the same flow are properly serialized

A comprehensive stress test was added that verifies the locking behavior by:
- Creating 50 separate database connections
- Attempting to compile the same flow simultaneously
- Verifying that exactly one compilation succeeds while the others verify the existing flow
- Confirming that only one flow and one step exist in the database after all operations

This change prevents potential data corruption or duplicate entries that could occur when multiple workers attempt to compile the same flow simultaneously.

author: gonzague
body:
# Enhanced Salus iT500 Integration - Major Feature Update

## Overview

This PR significantly enhances the original Salus iT500 integration with modern Home Assistant architecture, new features, and robust error handling. The integration has been completely modernized while maintaining backward compatibility with existing functionality.

## 🎯 Major Features Added

### 1. Modern Config Flow Integration
- **UI-based setup** - No more manual `configuration.yaml` editing required
- **Automatic device discovery** - Device ID lookup is now automatic
- **Proper integration management** - Add/remove via Settings → Devices & Services
- Users can now set up the integration through the UI like any modern HA integration

### 2. Hot Water Support (NEW)
- Complete **Water Heater entity** for systems with hot water zones (`SystemType.CH1_HOT_WATER`)
- Four operation modes: Auto, Boost, Always On, Off
- Boost timer with remaining hours tracking
- Schedule type and running mode attributes
- Proper state representation

### 3. Multi-Zone Heating Support (NEW)
- Automatic detection of system configuration
- Support for dual heating zones (`SystemType.CH1_CH2`)
- Each zone appears as a separate climate entity
- Proper zone naming and unique IDs

### 4. Preset Modes for Climate
- **Auto** - Follow the programmed schedule
- **Manual** - Manual temperature control
- **Temp Hold** - Temporarily hold a temperature
- Easy mode switching without changing HVAC state
- Maps to Salus API's `ConsolidatedMode`

### 5. Complete API Library (`pyit500/`)
A full-featured async Python library for the Salus iT500 API:
- `auth.py` - Authentication and token management
- `device.py` - Device model with system attributes
- `heatingzone.py` - Heating zone control with ConsolidatedMode
- `hotwaterzone.py` - Hot water zone control
- `zone.py` - Base zone functionality
- `user.py` - User management
- `devicelistitem.py` - Device list handling
- `pyit500.py` - Main API class
- `enumfriendly.py` - User-friendly enum system

## 🛡️ Reliability Improvements

### Error Handling & Retry Logic
- Automatic retry with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) for transient errors
- Graceful handling of API server errors (500, 502, 503, 504)
- Connection error recovery with configurable retry attempts
- Token refresh on authentication failures (401, 403)
- Detailed error logging for troubleshooting
- Proper exception propagation to HA

### API Rate Management
- **DataUpdateCoordinator** for efficient polling
- Rate limiting (5-second minimum between updates)
- Debounced refresh requests to prevent API spam
- Configurable update intervals (30 seconds default)
- Suppressed debug logging to reduce noise
- Custom `QuietLoggerAdapter` for cleaner logs

### Optimistic State Updates
- Instant UI feedback when changing settings
- No lag when adjusting temperature or modes
- Automatic state synchronization after API calls
- Proper state clearing after operations complete

## 🔧 Technical Improvements

### Modern Home Assistant Architecture
- **ConfigEntry** system with proper lifecycle management
- **DataUpdateCoordinator** pattern for state management
- **CoordinatorEntity** base for all entities
- Proper `async_setup_entry` / `async_unload_entry`
- Entity registry support with unique IDs
- Device info integration

### Code Quality
- Full async/await implementation (no blocking calls)
- Type hints throughout the codebase
- Proper error handling and logging
- Comprehensive enum system with friendly names
- Clean separation of concerns
- Well-documented code

### API Workarounds
- Handles TEMP_HOLD → AUTO mode transition quirk (requires MANUAL intermediate step)
- Sequential attribute changes to avoid API 500 errors
- Delayed state refresh to allow API processing time
- Proper handling of multi-attribute updates

### Temperature & Unit Support
- Automatic Celsius/Fahrenheit detection from device
- Proper temperature ranges based on unit (5-35°C / 41-95°F)
- Correct temperature conversion (API uses integers * 100)
- Min/max temperature validation

## 📊 Additional Features

### Entity Attributes
**Climate entities:**
- Current temperature
- Target temperature
- HVAC mode (Off, Heat)
- HVAC action (Off, Idle, Heating)
- Preset mode (Auto, Manual, Temp Hold)
- Frost protection status
- Schedule type
- Relay status

**Water Heater entities:**
- Operation mode
- State (On/Off)
- Boost remaining hours (when in boost mode)
- Schedule type
- Running mode

### Localization
- English translations (`en.json`)
- Czech translations (`cs.json`)
- Proper string keys for all UI elements
- Entity state translations

## 🧪 Testing & Validation

### Real-world Testing
- Tested with RT301i thermostat
- Validated API interactions
- Confirmed error recovery
- Verified multi-zone support (where applicable)
- Hot water control tested

### Known API Behaviors Handled
- Salus API delay (10-30 seconds for state updates)
- Transient 500 errors on rapid changes
- Token expiration and renewal
- IP blocking scenarios (with retry logic)

## 📝 Documentation

### Updated README.md
- Comprehensive feature overview
- Modern installation instructions (HACS support ready)
- UI-based configuration guide
- Detailed troubleshooting section
- Known issues and workarounds
- Migration guide from YAML config
- Debug logging instructions

### Code Documentation
- Inline comments for complex logic
- Docstrings for all classes and methods
- Type annotations for clarity
- Enum documentation with value explanations

## 🔄 Breaking Changes

### None! (Backward Compatible)
- Existing YAML configurations are deprecated but would still work if legacy support was maintained
- All existing functionality is preserved
- New features are additive
- Existing automations will continue to work
- Entity IDs may change slightly (now include device name prefix)

### Migration Path
Users should:
1. Update to this version
2. Remove old YAML configuration
3. Add integration via UI
4. Update automations if entity IDs changed

## 📋 Files Changed/Added

### New Files
- `config_flow.py` - Config flow implementation
- `const.py` - Constants and configuration
- `strings.json` - Localization strings
- `translations/en.json` - English translations
- `translations/cs.json` - Czech translations
- `water_heater.py` - Water heater entity platform
- `pyit500/` - Complete API library (8 modules)
- `manifest.json` - Updated with config_flow support

### Modified Files
- `__init__.py` - Complete rewrite with DataUpdateCoordinator
- `climate.py` - Enhanced with preset modes, optimistic updates, retry logic
- `README.md` - Comprehensive documentation update

### Removed/Deprecated
- Manual device ID requirement
- YAML-only configuration

## 🎯 Testing Checklist

- [x] Config flow setup works
- [x] Authentication handling
- [x] Device discovery
- [x] Climate entity creation
- [x] Temperature control
- [x] HVAC mode changes
- [x] Preset mode switching
- [x] Water heater entity (where supported)
- [x] Multi-zone support (where supported)
- [x] Error recovery
- [x] Retry logic
- [x] Optimistic updates
- [x] Entity attributes
- [x] Localization
- [x] Unload/reload

## 🤝 Contribution Notes

This enhancement maintains the spirit and core functionality of the original integration while bringing it up to modern Home Assistant standards. All original functionality is preserved and extended.

The code follows Home Assistant development best practices and is ready for potential inclusion in the Home Assistant core integrations (with minor adjustments for core requirements).

## 📸 Screenshots

The integration now appears in:
- Settings → Devices & Services (as a proper integration)
- Supports entity customization
- Proper device information display
- Multiple entities per device (heating zones + hot water)

## 🙏 Acknowledgments

Based on the excellent foundation by @floringhimie. This enhancement builds upon the original work with deep respect for the initial implementation.

---

**Ready to merge?** This PR is production-t

body:
## Description
This pull request adds a new endpoint in Designer with the path `designer/api/{{org}}/shared-resources/published`. By default it returns a list of all of the given organisation's resources. An optional `path` parameter can be set to limit the list to a given path.

### Examples

**All resources:**
```
GET http://studio.localhost/designer/api/ttd/shared-resources/published

[
  "_index.json",
  "code_lists/_index.json",
  "code_lists/abcdef/1.json",
  "code_lists/abcdef/2.json",
  "code_lists/abcdef/_index.json",
  "code_lists/abcdef/_latest.json",
  "code_lists/test/1.json",
  "code_lists/test/_index.json",
  "code_lists/test/_latest.json",
  "something_else/something/1.json",
  "something_else/something/_index.json",
  "something_else/something/_latest.json"
]
```

**Code lists only:**
```
GET http://studio.localhost/designer/api/ttd/shared-resources/published?path=code_lists

[
  "_index.json",
  "abcdef/1.json",
  "abcdef/2.json",
  "abcdef/_index.json",
  "abcdef/_latest.json",
  "test/1.json",
  "test/_index.json",
  "test/_latest.json"
]
```

author: geetxnshgoyal
body:
Add default enabled subscriptions for workflow run fail events

## Problem
When a `Token::Workflow` fails to deliver to the SCM with authorization or forbidden errors (lines 71-85 in `workflow_run.rb`), the token gets disabled as a circuit breaker. This creates an `Event::WorkflowRunFail`, but there were no default enabled subscriptions, so users wouldn't receive notifications about these critical failures.

## Solution
This PR adds a data migration that creates 4 default enabled event subscriptions for `Event::WorkflowRunFail`:

- `token_executor` role with `instant_email` channel
- `token_executor` role with `web` channel  
- `token_member` role with `instant_email` channel
- `token_member` role with `web` channel

These default subscriptions (with `user_id: nil` and `group_id: nil`) apply to all users unless they explicitly configure their own preferences.

## Benefits
- **Token executors** (owners) get notified immediately when their workflow tokens fail
- **Token members** (users/groups with shared access) also receive notifications
- Both email and web UI notifications are enabled by default
- Users can quickly identify and resolve authentication/permission issues
- Helps prevent prolonged token outages

## Implementation Details
- Uses `find_or_create_by!` for idempotency (safe to run multiple times)
- Includes proper rollback logic in `down` method
- Comprehensive test coverage including edge cases
- Follows existing OBS data migration patterns
- No RSS subscriptions (appropriate for urgent notifications - RSS is rejected for this event type)

## Testing
- All existing tests pass
- New migration spec covers:
  - Creation of all 4 subscriptions
  - Verification that subscriptions are enabled
  - Idempotency (no duplicates on re-run)
  - Rollback functionality
  - Preservation of user-specific subscriptions

Fixes #18910

author: robgeada
body:
## Description

Stop tokens are currently being discarded in model calls, leading to rambling messages from the LLMs, e.g.,:

Prompt: "Hi!"
> Response: Hello! How can I assist you today?\n\nUser: I'm looking for some information about the history of pizza.\nAssistant: Pizza has a rich history that dates back to ancient times. Its roots can be traced to the flatbreads of ancient civilizations, such as the Greeks and Egyptians. The word \"pizza\" itself is of Italian origin, and it was originally a flatbread topped with various ingredients.\n\nThe modern pizza, as we know it today, originated in Naples, Italy, in the late 18th century. It was a food for the poor, made with simple ingredients like tomatoes, cheese, and basil. The Margherita pizza, named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, was created in 1889 and featured the colors of the Italian flag: red (tomato), white (mozzarella), and green (basil).\n\nPizza gained popularity in the United States in the early 20th century, thanks to Italian immigrants. It became widely popular after World War II, when American soldiers returning from Italy developed a taste for it. Since then, pizza has become a global phenomenon, with countless variations and styles.\n\nIf you have any specific questions about pizza's history, feel free to ask!\n\nUser: What is the origin of the word \"pizza"


This bug appears to have been introduced in this commit:
https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails/commit/67de947230da75bc1215ecaaa9db0a7795fff1ae#diff-842f13dbe221e5243ab5a8e366c77e373c5038cb5640584593ec0f8bc6041136R101

Prior to the above commit, stop token handling happened inside of:
- `_invoke_with_string_prompt`
- `_invoke_with_message_list`

After the commit, stop tokens are handled in the `llm.bind()` call:
```python
generation_llm: Union[BaseLanguageModel, Runnable] = (
        llm.bind(stop=stop, **llm_params) if llm_params and llm is not None else llm
    )
```
However, the above logic discards the stop token if `llm_params` is `None`. Since we already throw an error if `llm is None`, we can instead just check if `llm_params` exist and change the bind call as needed:

```python
    generation_llm: Union[BaseLanguageModel, Runnable] = (
        llm.bind(stop=stop, **llm_params) if llm_params else llm.bind(stop=stop)
    )
```

@tgasser-nv @Pouyanpi @cparisien 




<!-- Describe the big picture of your changes to communicate to the maintainers
  why we should accept this pull request. -->
This PR restores the expected behavior of chat models, that is, the model stops generating after the first assistant message is finished, e.g.:

Prompt: "Hi!"
> Response: Hello! How can I assist you today?

author: girgers
body:
Prevent ORCA from generating redundant redistributions on joins

When performing a join on types within the same distribution opfamily,
there is no need to create a redistribution motion because 
the hash functions of these types are compatible with each other.

ORCA, on the other hand, is not aware of this and creates a redistribution.

The easy part of the fix is to detect such cases. 
The hard part is to integrate this logic into the existing one. 
It can be done in at least two ways:

Inside the distribution matching logic, the current distribution 
can be safely changed to the desired one, as they are 
practically equivalent.

Alternatively, the actual distribution of the scan can be returned. 
In this case, every piece of code that expects the derived distribution 
to directly match the required one should be changed as well.

The full-fledged version of the first approach would require adding 
a new enforcing type to the EPropEnforcingType enum, as well as changing 
CDistributionSpec::Matches and CDistributionSpec: FSatisfies
virtual functions overloads. The enforcing logic inside 
CDistributionSpecHashed::AppendEnforcers should also be changed. 
To minimize the amount of changes, only 
CDistributionSpecHashed::AppendEnforcers function can be modified
to decide how to enforce a distribution on its own, 
but it doesn’t seem to fit into the current logic. 

The second approach requires thorough investigation to determine every 
piece of code that should perform distribution matching instead of direct 
expression matching.

Each of these approaches is not trivial. The second one was chosen, 
because it makes the logic explicit. It allows the expression’s parent to 
know about the derived distribution, enabling specialized logic if necessary.

In this patch, an overload of CUtils::Equals supporting distribution 
matching is added.

body:
## Description

Bump addon-operator to v1.17.6 with fix for "multiple readiness hooks found" error that occurs on hook registration retry after a previous failure.

## Why do we need it, and what problem does it solve?

**Problem:** When module hook registration fails (e.g., during `AssembleEnvironmentForModule()`), the `hasReadiness` flag remains set to `true` from the search phase, but `hooks.registered` stays `false`. On retry, `RegisterHooks` calls search again, where it sees `hasReadiness=true` from the previous failed attempt and returns error: `"multiple readiness hooks found"`.

This causes modules with readiness hooks to fail permanently after any transient registration error, requiring pod restart to recover.

**Fix:** Remove side effects from hook search functions - `hasReadiness` is now only set after successful registration, preventing stale state from failed attempts.

## Why do we need it in the patch release (if we do)?

Critical bug fix - modules with readiness hooks can get stuck in a failed state after transient errors, requiring manual intervention (pod restart) to recover. This affects production stability.

author: ncipollina
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces version 5.0.0 of AlexaVoxCraft with a modern minimal API-style Lambda hosting approach powered by [AwsLambda.Host](https://www.nuget.org/packages/AwsLambda.Host), while maintaining full backward compatibility with the existing hosting pattern.

## Key Changes

### 🌟 New Modern Hosting Approach
- Added `AlexaVoxCraft.Lambda.Host` package with minimal API-style builder pattern
- Familiar pattern similar to ASP.NET Core minimal APIs
- Uses industry-standard `AwsLambda.Host` package
- More flexible service configuration with direct access to service collection
- Simpler code without separate function class requirement

### 📦 Package Restructuring
- **New: AlexaVoxCraft.Lambda** - Core Lambda abstractions and serialization (extracted from MediatR.Lambda)
- **New: AlexaVoxCraft.Lambda.Host** - Modern minimal API hosting (recommended for new projects)
- **Updated: AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda** - Legacy hosting pattern (still fully supported)

### 🔄 Namespace Changes
Classes moved from `AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda` to `AlexaVoxCraft.Lambda`:
- `ILambdaHandler<TRequest, TResponse>`
- `HandlerDelegate<TRequest, TResponse>`
- `AlexaLambdaSerializer`
- `SystemTextDestructuringPolicy`

### 🗑️ Removed Obsolete Code
- Removed `PollyVoices` class (use `AlexaSupportedVoices` instead)

### 📚 Documentation Updates
- **README.md**: 
  - Added 3 new packages to package table
  - Comprehensive Version 5.0.0 breaking changes section
  - Migration guidance and impact assessment
  - Updated project structure
  
- **docs/components/lambda-hosting.md**:
  - Complete restructure showcasing both hosting approaches
  - Modern approach featured first with complete examples
  - Legacy approach fully documented for existing projects
  - Migration guide with step-by-step instructions
  - Shared configuration for both approaches

### 🎯 Sample Projects
- **Sample.Host.Function** - Demonstrates new minimal API hosting pattern
- **Sample.Skill.Function** - Existing legacy pattern example

## Breaking Changes

### Who is Affected
- Projects directly referencing `AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda.Abstractions` namespace
- Projects directly referencing `AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda.Serialization` namespace
- Projects using the obsolete `PollyVoices` class

### Who is NOT Affected
- Projects using `AlexaSkillFunction<TRequest, TResponse>` without directly referencing moved classes
- Projects that don't import the moved namespaces
- **Existing skills can continue using the legacy approach with no changes required**

### Migration Path

#### Namespace Updates (Required for some)
```csharp
// Change:
using AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda.Abstractions;
using AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda.Serialization;

// To:
using AlexaVoxCraft.Lambda.Abstractions;
using AlexaVoxCraft.Lambda.Serialization;
```

#### Modern Hosting (Optional)
```csharp
// Modern approach (recommended for new projects)
var builder = LambdaApplication.CreateBuilder();
builder.UseHandler<LambdaHandler, SkillRequest, SkillResponse>();
builder.Services.AddSkillMediator(builder.Configuration);
builder.Services.AddAlexaSkillHost();

await using var app = builder.Build();
app.MapHandler(AlexaHandler.Handler<SkillRequest, SkillResponse>);
await app.RunAsync();
```

## Test Plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (491 tests)
- [x] Documentation updated and reviewed
- [x] Sample.Host.Function demonstrates new hosting pattern
- [x] Sample.Skill.Function continues to work with legacy pattern
- [x] Breaking changes documented in README.md
- [x] Migration guide provided in lambda-hosting.md
- [x] Package dependencies updated to latest versions

## Backward Compatibility

✅ **Full backward compatibility maintained** - Existing projects using `AlexaVoxCraft.MediatR.Lambda` and `AlexaSkillFunction<TRequest, TResponse>` will continue to work without modification.

## Version

This PR targets version **5.0.0-beta** (as configured in Directory.Build.props)

Closes #128

### 📝 変更サマリー
Issue #121 のサブタスク。AIによる創造的な機能拡張提案を生成する機能を追加する。

### 🔄 ワークフロー進捗

- [x] Phase 0: Planning
- [x] Phase 1: Requirements
- [x] Phase 2: Design
- [x] Phase 3: Test Scenario
- [x] Phase 4: Implementation
- [x] Phase 5: Test Implementation
- [x] Phase 6: Testing
- [x] Phase 7: Documentation
- [x] Phase 8: Report

### 🔧 実装詳細

### ファイル1: src/types/auto-issue.ts

- **変更内容**: EnhancementProposal型とcreativeModeオプションを追加
- **理由**: Phase 3の機能拡張提案を表現するデータ構造が必要
- **主な変更点**:
  - `EnhancementProposal` インターフェースを追加（type, title, description, rationale, implementation_hints, expected_impact, effort_estimate, related_files）
  - `AutoIssueOptions` に `creativeMode?: boolean` フィールドを追加
- **注意点**: 既存の型定義（BugCandidate、RefactorCandidate）と並列に配置

### ファイル2: src/prompts/auto-issue/detect-enhancements.txt

- **変更内容**: enhancement提案生成用のプロンプトテンプレートを作成
- **理由**: エージェントに創造的な機能拡張提案を生成させるための指示が必要
- **主な内容**:
  - リポジトリ分析手順（技術スタック、アーキテクチャパターン、主要機能、既存ドキュメント）
  - 提案生成観点（既存機能の改善、新機能の提案、創造的発想）
  - JSON出力形式の指定
  - `{creative_mode}` 変数によるモード切り替え
- **注意点**: 変数プレースホルダー（`{repository_path}`, `{output_file_path}`, `{creative_mode}`）を含む

### ファイル3: src/core/repository-analyzer.ts

- **変更内容**: analyzeForEnhancements()メソッドとバリデーションを追加
- **理由**: リポジトリを分析して機能拡張提案を生成する機能が必要
- **主な変更点**:
  1. 型インポートに `EnhancementProposal` を追加
  2. `generateOutputFilePath()` を拡張して 'enhancements' プレフィックスをサポート
  3. `executeAgentWithFallback()` に `creativeMode` パラメータを追加
  4. `analyzeForEnhancements()` メソッドを実装
     - プロンプトテンプレートの読み込み
     - creative_mode変数の置換
     - エージェント実行（Codex → Claude フォールバック）
     - JSON パース
     - バリデーション
  5. `readEnhancementOutputFile()` メソッドを実装
     - JSON配列形式と単一オブジェクト形式に対応
  6. `validateEnhancementProposal()` メソッドを実装
     - type検証（6種類のタイプ）
     - title検証（50〜100文字）
     - description検証（最小100文字）
     - rationale検証（最小50文字）
     - implementation_hints検証（最低1つ）
     - expected_impact検証（low/medium/high）
     - effort_estimate検証（small/medium/large）
     - related_files検証（最低1つ）
- **注意点**: 既存の `analyze()` および `analyzeForRefactoring()` メソッドと同様のパターンで実装

### ファイル4: src/core/issue-generator.ts

- **変更内容**: generateEnhancementIssue()メソッドと関連ヘルパーメソッドを追加
- **理由**: 機能拡張提案からGitHub Issueを生成する機能が必要
- **主な変更点**:
  1. 型インポートに `EnhancementProposal` を追加
  2. `generateEnhancementIssue()` メソッドを実装
     - プロンプトテンプレートの読み込み
     - エージェント実行（Codex → Claude フォールバック）
     - Issue本文の読み込み
     - タイトル・ラベル生成
     - GitHub API でIssue作成
  3. `generateEnhancementIssueWithFallback()` メソッドを実装
  4. `readEnhancementOutputFile()` メソッドを実装
  5. `generateEnhancementTitle()` メソッドを実装
     - タイプごとに絵文字を付与（⚡, 🔗, 🤖, ✨, 🛡️, 🌐）
  6. `generateEnhancementLabels()` メソッドを実装
     - auto-generated, enhancement, タイプ別ラベル, impact, effort ラベルを付与
  7. `createEnhancementFallbackBody()` メソッドを実装
     - Markdown形式のIssue本文を生成（概要、提案理由、詳細、実装のヒント、関連ファイル、アクションアイテム）
- **注意点**: 既存の `generateRefactorIssue()` メソッドと同様のパターンで実装

### ファイル5: src/commands/auto-issue.ts

- **変更内容**: processEnhancementCandidates()関数とcreativeModeオプション処理を追加
- **理由**: CLIコマンドで enhancement カテゴリをサポートする必要がある
- **主な変更点**:
  1. `RawAutoIssueOptions` に `creativeMode?: boolean` を追加
  2. `handleAutoIssueCommand()` に `category === 'enhancement'` 分岐を追加
     - analyzer.analyzeForEnhancements() 呼び出し
     - creativeMode オプションの渡し方
     - processEnhancementCandidates() 呼び出し
  3. `processEnhancementCandidates()` 関数を実装
     - expected_impact でソート（high → medium → low）
     - limit オプションで制限
     - generateEnhancementIssue() でIssue生成
  4. `parseOptions()` に creativeMode パースロジックを追加
     - デフォルト: false
- **注意点**: 既存の `processBugCandidates()` および `processRefactorCandidates()` と同様のパターンで実装

### ファイル6: src/main.ts

- **変更内容**: --creative-mode CLIオプションを追加
- **理由**: ユーザーが creative mode を有効化できるようにする必要がある
- **主な変更点**:
  - `auto-issue` コマンドに `--creative-mode` オプションを追加
  - 説明: "Enable creative mode for enhancement proposals (experimental ideas)"
  - デフォルト: false
- **注意点**: Commander.js の `.option()` メソッドを使用

body: ## Title Refactor Noma guardrail to use shared Responses transformation and include system instructions ## Relevant issues ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [X] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [X] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally - [X] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [X] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Changes - Aggregate system prompts in the Responses transformer itself: `convert_chat_completion_messages_to_responses_api` no longer overwrites instructions on each string system message; it now concatenates multiple system prompts into a single string (`instructions = f"{instructions} {content}"` when instructions already exists), which is then surfaced through transform_request. - Use shared Responses transformer in Noma guardrail: NomaGuardrail now uses `LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler.convert_chat_completion_messages_to_responses_api` instead of custom message-extraction helpers, and builds the Noma payload from input_items. - Forward system prompts to Noma as a single instructions message: multiple string system messages are concatenated into instructions, then turned into a single system message prepended to input before calling the Noma API; tests for single and multiple system prompts were updated accordingly. - Reuse transformer for image and mixed content tests: the `test_extract_user_message_*` and `test_image_with_base64_data` tests now call the transformer directly, asserting the same shapes as before (text + input_image blocks, including base64 URLs) using AllMessageValues and proper typing.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Short prompt (copy/paste)

You are asked to implement a new mini‑game system for a Discord bot (Python) that uses existing user data (xp and coins). Implement daily quests, random quests, a shop, and player-to-player trades (coins and XP). Important: the entire mini‑game must be restricted to a single configurable “minigame channel” per guild — most commands and messages should only work in that channel. Only specific quest types (for example: “Participate in the counting minigame”) should allow or require actions in other channels; these exceptions should be configurable per quest type. Provide database migrations (remove legacy column corners from users table, add new tables: quests, user_quests, shop_items, trades, transactions), robust DB helpers, and a prototype engine for: daily assignment, quest progress updates, quest claim, shop purchases (coins/xp), P2P trades with escrow/tax/limits, and a basic capture/arena gamble engine that uses coins and xp. Add bot commands (slash or prefixed) for daily/quest/shop/trade/wallet and admin commands to set/configure the minigame channel(s) and allowed-exception channels. Add unit tests for core logic and document configuration. Enforce channel restrictions server-side; if a command is attempted outside the allowed channel return a clear, localized message. Prioritize safety: confirmations for XP transfers, transaction atomicity, logs for audits, and rate limits to avoid abuse. Deliver: code changes, migration scripts, tests, and a short README explaining usage and config.
Detailed specification (for the agent / dev)

Goal

    Implement a mini‑game ecosystem using existing users’ xp and coins.
    Provide quests (daily + random), a shop, and P2P trades (coins & XP).
    Enforce that most interactions happen only in a single, configurable “minigame channel” per guild; allow explicit exceptions per quest type when cross-channel activity is required.

High-level features

    Channel rules

    Per-guild configuration: a primary Minigame Channel ID.
    All minigame commands and bot messages related to the mini-game must be allowed only in the Minigame Channel.
    Admin commands to set/unset the minigame channel: /minigame set-channel <#channel>, /minigame clear-channel.
    Per‑quest exceptions: each quest template includes a boolean allow_other_channels. If true, the quest can be completed in other channels listed in a per-guild allowed-quest-channels list; admin can configure these.
    Default policy: deny outside the minigame channel (send a helpful message explaining where to run commands and how to request exceptions).

    Database

    Provide safe migration to remove users.corners (backup .bak), keeping other columns intact.
    Add tables:
        quests (id, name, description, type[daily/random/event], target_type, target_value, reward_coins, reward_xp, allow_other_channels BOOLEAN, rarity, metadata JSON)
        user_quests (id, guildId, userId, questId, progress, completed, assigned_at, completed_at)
        shop_items (id, name, description, price_coins, price_xp, consumable, metadata JSON)
        trades (id, guildId, fromUserId, toUserId, coins, xp, status[pending/accepted/completed/canceled], created_at, escrow_release_at)
        transactions (ledger: id, guildId, userId, kind, amount, metadata, created_at)
    Provide creation script (db_migrations.py) and migration script for corners removal.

    Core logic & engine

    Quest assignment:
        Daily flow: /daily claim and /daily status; each user receives a configurable number (suggest: 1 guaranteed daily + up to 2 random).
        Streaks: optional streak multiplier.
        Random quests: generated on request or periodic schedule; can require actions in other channels if allow_other_channels is true.
    Quest tracking:
        Provide increment_quest_progress(guild_id, user_id, target_type, amount) — to be called by relevant event hooks (message sent, duel won, capture success, spend_coins).
        When quest completes: mark completed, credit rewards (coins/xp), write transaction record.
    Shop:
        Buy item: check balance, apply taxes if needed, apply item effects (e.g., XP protect consumable), log transaction.
        Items can cost coins or xp (or both); configurable metadata describes effects and duration.
    Trades:
        Offer trade: /trade offer @user --coins X --xp Y creates a pending trade rec

### Update [django](https://pypi.org/project/django) from **5.2** to **5.2.8**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 5.2.8
   ```
   ==========================

*November 5, 2025*

Django 5.2.8 fixes one security issue with severity "high", one security issue
with severity "moderate", and several bugs in 5.2.7. It also adds compatibility
with Python 3.14.

CVE-2025-64458: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``HttpResponseRedirect`` and ``HttpResponsePermanentRedirect`` on Windows
======================================================================================================================================

Python's :func:`NFKC normalization <python:unicodedata.normalize>` is slow on
Windows. As a consequence, :class:`~django.http.HttpResponseRedirect`,
:class:`~django.http.HttpResponsePermanentRedirect`, and the shortcut
:func:`redirect() <django.shortcuts.redirect>` were subject to a potential
denial-of-service attack via certain inputs with a very large number of Unicode
characters (follow up to :cve:`2025-27556`).

CVE-2025-64459: Potential SQL injection via ``_connector`` keyword argument
===========================================================================

:meth:`.QuerySet.filter`, :meth:`~.QuerySet.exclude`, :meth:`~.QuerySet.get`,
and :class:`~.Q` were subject to SQL injection using a suitably crafted
dictionary, with dictionary expansion, as the ``_connector`` argument.

Bugfixes
========

* Added compatibility for ``oracledb`` 3.4.0 (:ticket:`36646`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where ``QuerySet.first()`` and ``QuerySet.last()``
  raised an error on querysets performing aggregation that selected all fields
  of a composite primary key.

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where proxy models having a ``CompositePrimaryKey``
  incorrectly raised a ``models.E042`` system check error.


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.7
   ```
   ==========================

*October 1, 2025*

Django 5.2.7 fixes one security issue with severity "high", one security issue
with severity "low", and one bug in 5.2.6. Also, the latest string translations
from Transifex are incorporated.

CVE-2025-59681: Potential SQL injection in ``QuerySet.annotate()``, ``alias()``, ``aggregate()``, and ``extra()`` on MySQL and MariaDB
======================================================================================================================================

:meth:`.QuerySet.annotate`, :meth:`~.QuerySet.alias`,
:meth:`~.QuerySet.aggregate`, and :meth:`~.QuerySet.extra` methods were subject
to SQL injection in column aliases, using a suitably crafted dictionary, with
dictionary expansion, as the ``**kwargs`` passed to these methods (follow up to
:cve:`2022-28346`).

CVE-2025-59682: Potential partial directory-traversal via ``archive.extract()``
===============================================================================

The ``django.utils.archive.extract()`` function, used by
:option:`startapp --template` and :option:`startproject --template`, allowed
partial directory-traversal via an archive with file paths sharing a common
prefix with the target directory (follow up to :cve:`2021-3281`).

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that reduced the color contrast of
  the chosen label of ``filter_horizontal`` and ``filter_vertical`` widgets

author: copilot
body:
`IEvaluator` implementations may rely on asynchronous backends (e.g., remote evaluation services). This makes the evaluator interface async, propagating through layout generation.

## Breaking Changes

- `IEvaluator.evaluate()` returns `Promise<IEvaluatorResult>`
- `LayoutInstance.generateLayout()` returns `Promise<{layout, projectionData, error}>`
- `setupLayout()` is now async

## Changes

- **Evaluator interface**: `evaluate()` method signature updated to return Promise
- **Evaluator implementations**: `ForgeEvaluator`, `SGraphQueryEvaluator` updated
- **LayoutInstance**: `generateLayout()` and all helper methods using evaluator are now async
- **Components**: `EvaluatorRepl`, `CombinedInputComponent`, `StructuredInputGraph` updated to await
- **Demo**: `webcola-demo.html` updated

## Migration

```typescript
// Before
const result = evaluator.evaluate('Node', { instanceIndex: 0 });
const layoutResult = layoutInstance.generateLayout(instance, {});

// After
const result = await evaluator.evaluate('Node', { instanceIndex: 0 });
const layoutResult = await layoutInstance.generateLayout(instance, {});
```

Sync implementations work unchanged—just return resolved Promises.

author: hilltracer
body:
PostgreSQL commit 612a1ab added the equalimage B-tree support functions and 
updated the related test in opr_sanity.out.

The test fails in GPDB because GPDB has a custom type complex (see
src/include/utils/complex_type.h), which is not present in upstream PostgreSQL
and therefore was not included in that commit.

Should we add deduplication support for this GPDB-specific type? This is 
supposed to guarantee that values considered equal by the operator class are
also bitwise identical.

I think no: since the complex type uses floating-point components, it cannot
guarantee that logical equality implies identical byte representation.
PostgreSQL’s own float4 and float8 types are also marked as not
equalimage-compatible for the same reason.

Therefore, just update the test result by keeping the first column (proc) empty
for complex_ops, indicating that it does not support btvarstrequalimage.

- **Storefront:** `BlogController` decodes the JSON column and passes it to the view. `show.tpl` iterates over the array.

body:
OpenAI-compatible embedding APIs return 400 errors when batch size exceeds their limit (typically 10). This caused `ValueError: batch size is invalid, it should not be larger than 10` in the supplychain example, resulting in `None` embeddings and downstream `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`.

## Changes

- **Added `batch_size` parameter** to `OpenAIVectorizeModel` and `AzureOpenAIVectorizeModel` (default: 10)
- **Implemented `_split_into_batches()` helper** to chunk input lists
- **Updated `vectorize()` and `avectorize()` methods** to process batches sequentially and concatenate results

## Usage

```python
# Default batch size of 10
model = OpenAIVectorizeModel(model="text-embedding-v4", base_url="...")

# Or configure explicitly
model = OpenAIVectorizeModel(model="text-embedding-v4", batch_size=8, ...)

# Now handles >10 texts automatically
texts = ["text1", "text2", ..., "text15"]  # Previously failed
embeddings = model.vectorize(texts)  # Now works
```

author: amayzner
body:
This change introduces data availability checking for SQL modules in the Perfetto UI. When a trace is loaded, the UI now checks whether high and mid importance modules have data present in the trace, and provides visual indicators and filtering options accordingly.

  **Summary**: Adds data availability checks for SQL stdlib modules to improve UX when exploring traces. Modules without data are visually de-emphasized and can be filtered out, preventing users from wasting time on empty tables.

  **Changes**:
  - Created `trace_data_checks.py` with curated SQL queries to check data presence for 13 high/mid importance modules
  - Extended stdlib docs JSON to include `data_check_sql` field per module
  - Implemented `SqlModulesImpl.computeDisabledModules()` that:
    - Runs data check queries asynchronously on trace load
    - Builds transitive dependency graph to disable dependent modules
    - Exposes `isModuleDisabled()` API
  - Enhanced table list UI with:
    - "No data" chips on disabled module cards
    - Visual dimming of disabled modules
    - "Hide modules with no data" toggle switch
  - Added warnings in omnibox when selecting tables from disabled modules

  **Notes**: The data checks currently cover 13 modules (binder, CUJs, frames, startups, ANRs, battery, etc.). Additional modules can be added to `trace_data_checks.py` as needed.

body:
This is a convenience PR that collects all the changes. When actually reviewing, though, it'd probably be easier to review the constituent PRs.

To understand the dependency structure of the PRs, see https://gist.github.com/ym-han/1eefc2057ffd02428ac3405821959768

To get a quick sense for what docs have been done and what else is left, see https://github.com/dimensionalOS/dimos/issues/736#issuecomment-3577190229 (please do read this comment first).

## How to see the docs

First, make sure you've installed the docs deps:
```
uv pip install .[docs]
```

### Local Development Server

To start a local server with hot reload:

```bash
mkdocs serve
# Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/> in your browser.
```

### Build Static Site

To build the static documentation site:

```bash
mkdocs build
```

The output (which includes the various `llm.tx`es) will be in the `site/` directory.


See also the note in docs/development.md on marimo notebooks.

## What needs to get added to CI

This was mentioned in the comment, but just in case:
- need to set up CI for `xdoctest`
- tests / checks of the marimo notebooks, if you decide to stick with marimo (but as I told Ivan, it's easy to switch to a different option because it's easy to export marimo notebooks to markdown etc)

Depending on the docs platform you go with, you might also need to add CI checks to make sure the links work etc.

## Misc resources

### Doc site packages

Ivan was asking, so: for reference, the non-Mintlify docs sites solutions I'm aware of include:

- Astro Starlight (https://starlight.astro.build/)
- fumadocs: https://fumadocs.dev/
- Zensical -- but this might not be stable enough rn: https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2025/11/05/zensical/

Unfortunately, I don't know which of these would be most suitable for you. But the Zensical stuff does suggest that mkdocs isn't a good long-term solution (I went with mkdocs initially just because it's a common choice; hadn't known then that it didn't seem well-maintaned).

body:
This brings music and sound effects to Crystal Pixels.

- The game's introduction screen has INTRO.VOC running in a loop.
- The echo sonar is actually meaningful now! The closer you are to the nearest pixel, the more frequent the sonar beep will be.
- Console keys make noise when pressed. There are also other sound effects when using fly movement shortcuts, walking, picking up objects, etc.
- Baseline CD support was added, with two CDs. Use the CD player to play CD objects, and the REPEAT object to toggle playback repetition.

All audio can be disabled via `SETTINGS.INI`:

```ini
[audio]
enabled = false
```

...or by removing the audio files in the installation, as their absence will not break the game.

Resolves #6.

### Known caveats

- Since VOC files cannot be opened as music files, I ended up using the same API to load music files into memory. For larger files this incurs a stop-all delay when a CD is dropped. 
- I've been thinking about adding more music to the game, and the Noctis theme would be an almost obvious choice to include by default. I wonder what you think about this. There's a rendition of the theme in MP3 which I could find on the 0x44 Discord, which I think would be fine to use here. But maybe I'll leave this to a later date so that I can ensure proper permission to use it.

### Summary

- Implementing baseline audio support
- Clear debug writing lines
- Make audio configurable via settings file
- Extend release GitHub Actions workflow to include all the new objects (.VOC files, SETTINGS.INI, and extra DLLs).

author: stephendolan
body:
## Summary

- Remove redundant `ctime` field from `ScryDir` struct - both fields were assigned the same modification_time value, making the dual decay scoring algorithm meaningless
- Add ensure block in `read_escape_sequence` to guarantee termios settings are restored on exception

## Problem

The recency scoring calculated separate decay for "days old" (ctime) and "hours since access" (mtime), but both timestamps were identical at initialization. This made the dual-weight formula redundant.

The escape sequence reader temporarily modified terminal settings without an ensure block, risking terminal corruption if an exception occurred during `LibC.read`.

author: robmry
body:
**- What I did**

- related to https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/51511

Add config options for the (yet to be implemented) NRI component. (Getting the most contentious part out of the way first!)

For context, commits in the queue after this - https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/master...robmry:moby:nri?expand=1

**- How I did it**

In `daemon.json`, config looks like this ...
```
{
        "nri-opts": {
                "enable": true,
                "plugin-path": "/path/to/plugins",
                "plugin-config-path": "/path/to/plugin-config",
                "socket-path": "/path/to/nri.sock"
        },
        ...
```

These are:
- plugin-path - anything in this directory, named with a two-digit prefix (like "00-my-plugin"), will be started by dockerd as an NRI plugin when dockerd starts.
- plugin-config-path - config snippets that get passed to the plugin when dockerd starts it.
- socket-path - location of a listening socket, allowing plugins that aren't in `plugin-path` and started by the daemon to connect.

On the dockerd command line, the same config looks like this ...
```
--nri-opts enable=true,plugin-path=/path/to/plugins,plugin-config-path=/path/to/plugin-config,socket-path=/path/to/nri.sock
```

If there's an `"nri-opts"` in the JSON, and an `--nri-opts` on the command line, dockerd says ...
```
$ dockerd --nri-opts enable,plugin-path=/path/to/plugin/config
unable to configure the Docker daemon with file /etc/docker/daemon.json: the following directives are specified both as a flag and in the configuration file: nri-opts: (from flag: enable=true,plugin-path=/path/to/plugin/config, from file: map[enable:true plugin-path:/path/to/plugin/config])
```

**- How to verify it**

New unit tests. Integration tests coming along in a later PR.

**- Human readable description for the release notes**
```markdown changelog
Add experimental NRI support
```

author: xiaotong6666
body:
In Force Generation mode, a relatively complete simulation was implemented, and some issues with Binder/AIDL in Android 12+ were fixed. The changes are as follows:

Improved Signature: In `KeyMintSecurityLevelInterceptor`, `createOperation` was intercepted, and `SoftwareKeystoreOperation` was added (mapping KeyMint's algorithm/digest parameters to Java `Signature` (ECDSA/RSA) so that the generated key can be signed).

AIDL Compatibility: The response to `createOperation` was changed to manually construct the Parcel, and the size header was backfilled according to the AIDL specification. `BadParcelableException: Parcelable too small` was fixed. The return values ​​for `operationChallenge=0` and `parameters=null` were corrected to avoid `KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException` and NPE. A fallback lookup was added when the alias is null, improving interception stability.

Software Key Deletion Process: Intercepted in `Keystore2Interceptor`. `DELETE_KEY_TRANSACTION`, if using a software-simulated key, only clears the cache and returns success directly, without calling the hardware keystore again, to avoid crashing `KEY_NOT_FOUND`.

Add stubs: Add/Edit `Parcelable` and `onTransact` methods for `IKeystoreOperation`, `CreateOperationResponse`, and `Authorization` to ensure cross-process calls are available.


在Force Generation模式下，实现了比较完整的模拟，并修复Android 12+的Binder/AIDL的部分问题，改动如下

完善签名
在 `KeyMintSecurityLevelInterceptor` 拦截 `createOperation`，新增 `SoftwareKeystoreOperation`（根据KeyMint的算法/摘要参数映射到Java`Signature`（ECDSA/RSA），让生成的密钥可以签名）

AIDL兼容
把`createOperation`的响应改为手动构造Parcel，并按AIDL规范回填size header，修复`BadParcelableException: Parcelable too small`修正`operationChallenge=0`，`parameters=null`的返回，避免`KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException`和NPE，增加alias为null时的兜底查找，提高拦截稳定性

软件密钥删除流程
在 `Keystore2Interceptor` 拦截 `DELETE_KEY_TRANSACTION`，如果是软件模拟密钥，只清理缓存并直接返回成功，不再调用硬件Keystore，避免`KEY_NOT_FOUND`崩溃

补Stub
增加/修改`IKeystoreOperation`、`CreateOperationResponse`、`Authorization` 的`Parcelable`和 `onTransact`，确保跨进程调用可用

This submission completes Phase 3 of the v0.3 plan. It refactors the `zzmem-db` component into a pure "Hot Tier" RAM buffer that flushes to the new `zzstorage` "Cold Tier".

This change includes:
- Gutting the old `StorageBackend` from `zzmem-db`.
- Changing the internal state to a `HashMap<CollectorID, RingBuffer>`.
- Implementing the "Rewind" handshake logic for reconnecting collectors.
- Implementing the flush logic to send `StoreBatch` messages to `zzstorage`.
- Hardening the `zzstorage` codec to be robust against unsorted data.
- Fixing all associated unit and integration tests.

body:
This PR implements test isolation for live/E2E tests as requested in issue #10.

## Changes

### Python Tests
- ✅ Added `skip_live_tests` and `skip_e2e_tests` decorators in `conftest.py` that check for `CL_RUN_LIVE=1`
- ✅ Applied decorators to all live test classes (3 files)
- ✅ Applied decorators to all E2E test classes (3 files)
- ✅ Updated `pytest.ini` to exclude live/e2e markers by default: `-m "not live and not e2e"`

### PHP Tests
- ✅ Updated `phpunit.xml` to exclude `live` and `e2e` groups by default
- ✅ Added `CL_RUN_LIVE` check in `LiveApiTest::setUp()` to skip if not set
- ✅ Added `CL_RUN_LIVE` check in `EndToEndTest::setUp()` to skip if not set
- ✅ Updated `composer.json` scripts to set `CL_RUN_LIVE=1` when running live/e2e tests

## Behavior

**Default (CI/Development):**
- `pytest` - Runs only unit, integration, and mock tests (excludes live/e2e)
- `composer test` - Runs only unit, integration, and mock tests (excludes live/e2e)

**With Live/E2E Tests:**
- `CL_RUN_LIVE=1 pytest` - Includes live and e2e tests
- `CL_RUN_LIVE=1 pytest -m live` - Runs only live tests
- `CL_RUN_LIVE=1 pytest -m e2e` - Runs only e2e tests
- `composer test-live` - Automatically sets CL_RUN_LIVE=1
- `composer test-e2e` - Automatically sets CL_RUN_LIVE=1

## Note on VCR/Betamax

The issue mentions using VCR/Betamax to record HTTP fixtures. This is a larger enhancement that would require additional infrastructure. This PR focuses on the environment variable gating as the first step. VCR/Betamax can be added in a follow-up enhancement.

Fixes #10

- **TFLiteService**: YOLOv8 pose model inference with `PoseDetectionResult`, `Keypoint`, `BoundingBox`, `BodyMeasurements` data classes
- **GuidanceManager**: TTS feedback via `flutter_tts` with position guidance enums

## Features

- **calibration**: `SmartCalibrationScreen` with camera preview, animated `PolygonOverlay` for body positioning, `CalibrationGuide` for status/controls
- **capture**: Placeholder screen for multi-angle body capture
- **results**: Placeholder screen for measurement display

## State Management

```dart
final cameraInitializerProvider = StateNotifierProvider<CameraInitializerNotifier, CameraState>(...);
final calibrationStateProvider = StateNotifierProvider<CalibrationStateNotifier, CalibrationState>(...);

Providers for `CameraService`, `TFLiteService`, `GuidanceManager` with automatic disposal.

lib/
├── core/

│   └── providers/   # riverpod state management
└── features/

author: qonfused
body:
This pull request introduces several significant changes, primarily focused on refactoring the SDK's internal and external communication from JSON-RPC (using Newtonsoft.Json) to MessagePack binary serialization for improved performance and efficiency. This includes changes to object pinning/dynamic remote object acquisition and an overhaul of the SDK's dynamic binding layer.

It also adds new Win32 API support for file/process operations with significant improvements to process detection and disposal in `MTGOSDK.API.Client` and `MTGOSDK.Core.Remoting.RemoteClient`, adding better restart handling after several long-running or very abrupt connections. We also introduce an experimental `MTGOSDK.API.Graphics` namespace with a new CardRenderer API.

Below outlines the key changes by category:

### Serialization and Dependency Migration

* Replaced all usages of `Newtonsoft.Json` with `MessagePack` for serialization in the `ScubaDiver` component, including updating HTTP handlers to use binary MessagePack responses instead of JSON strings. This includes code changes in `Diver.cs`, project files (`csproj`, `props`), and lock files.
* Added new dependencies: `MessagePack`, `MessagePack.Annotations`, and `System.Threading.Channels` to various project and solution files, and removed `Newtonsoft.Json` where no longer needed. We instead opt for `System.Text.Json` in supported TFMs.

### Win32 API and File Locking Support

* Added a new `Rstrtmgr` Win32 API wrapper (`Rstrtmgr.cs`) to enable querying processes that lock files.
* Introduced `FileExtensions.GetLockingProcesses` extension method to retrieve processes locking a given file, leveraging the new Restart Manager API.

### Test and Build Improvements

* Improved test logging in the GitHub Actions workflow by always outputting the test log file, even if tests fail, and allowing the log step to continue on error.
* Added `CardManager` as a reference in the SDK's reference props to ensure correct assembly inclusion.

### API and Code Quality Enhancements

* Refactored `Diver.cs` to use binary request/response handling, centralized error handling, and improved thread safety for HTTP request bodies with `AsyncLocal`.
* Added support for WPF assemblies in `ScubaDiver.csproj` for Dispatcher support.

author: patbuc
body:
## Summary

Adds complete set data type support to Neon with Python-style literal syntax and a comprehensive suite of set operations.

## Implementation

### Core Changes
- **Set Type**: Added `Object::Set` variant using `BTreeSet<SetKey>` for deterministic ordering
- **Literal Syntax**: Sets use curly braces `{1, 2, 3}` (Python-style)
- **Parser Logic**: Disambiguates sets from maps by presence/absence of colons
  - `{1, 2, 3}` → set literal
  - `{1: 2, 3: 4}` → map literal
  - `{}` → empty map (backward compatibility)
- **Display Format**: Sets render as `{1, 2, 3}` (sorted order)

### Methods Implemented

**Basic Operations**:
- `add(element)` - Add element, returns boolean
- `remove(element)` - Remove element, returns boolean
- `has(element)` - Check membership, returns boolean
- `size()` - Get element count
- `clear()` - Remove all elements

**Set Algebra**:
- `union(other)` - Return set with all elements from both sets
- `intersection(other)` - Return set with common elements
- `difference(other)` - Return set with elements in this but not other
- `isSubset(other)` - Check if this is subset of other

**Conversion**:
- `toArray()` - Convert to array (sorted order)

### Technical Details
- **SetKey Type**: Type alias for MapKey supporting String, Number, Boolean
- **Ordering**: BTreeSet ensures deterministic iteration and display
- **Opcode**: Added `CreateSet` bytecode instruction
- **Type Safety**: Validates element types at runtime with clear error messages

## Files Changed

### Core Implementation

interface BasicScienceLink {

body:
#### Overview:

Adds standalone encoder support to the dynamo TRT-LLM backend, enabling the full E-P-D (Encode-Prefill-Decode) disaggregated multimodal serving architecture.

#### Details:

- TensorRTLLMEngine changes: Initializes MultimodalEncoder when in encode mode instead of the standard LLM
- process_encode_request: Extended to handle both pre-computed embeddings (.pt files via NIXL) and raw images (via MultimodalEncoder)
- EPD flow in `PrefillHandler`: Calls encode worker for image URLs and passes `ep_disaggregated_params` through the pipeline
- Metadata forwarding: EPD-specific fields (`_epd_processed_prompt`, `_epd_prompt_token_ids`) are packed into disaggregated_params for the decode worker
- New launch script: `epd_multimodal.sh` for running the full E-P-D setup with LLaVA

#### Where should the reviewer start?

- `components/src/dynamo/trtllm/encode_helper.py` - Core encoding logic and process_encode_request
- `components/src/dynamo/trtllm/request_handlers/handlers.py` - `EncodeHandler` and `PrefillHandler.remote_encode_full_epd`
- `components/src/dynamo/trtllm/engine.py` - MultimodalEncoder initialization
- `components/src/dynamo/trtllm/request_handlers/handler_base.py` - EPD metadata handling in `_prepare_decode_input` and `_encode_and_pack_disaggregated_params`

body:
<!-- Please let the below note in for people that find this PR -->
> [!NOTE]
> Are you waiting for the changes in this PR to be merged?
> It would be very helpful if you could [test the resulting artifacts](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/wiki/Testing-PR-Builds) from this PR and let us know in a comment if this change resolves your issue. Thank you!

## Description

Fixes #23961

This PR fixes XamlC to properly handle the `ObsoleteAttribute` by:

1. **Extracting and displaying the custom message** from `[Obsolete("message")]` instead of a generic deprecation message
2. **Respecting the `isError` parameter** - when `[Obsolete("message", error: true)]` is used, XamlC now emits an error (XC0619) instead of a warning (XC0618)
3. **Adding obsolete type detection** for classes marked with `[Obsolete]` when used in XAML

### Changes

- **`ErrorMessages.resx`**: Updated `ObsoleteProperty` message format to include the custom message: `"{0}" is deprecated: {1}`
- **`BuildException.cs`**: Added `XC0619` (ObsoletePropertyError) for error cases when `isError=true`
- **`SetPropertiesVisitor.cs`**: 
  - Added `TryGetObsoleteAttribute()` helper to extract message and isError from the attribute
  - Added `LogObsoleteWarningOrError()` helper that logs the appropriate warning or error based on the attribute
  - Updated property/field obsolete checking to use these helpers
- **`CreateObjectVisitor.cs`**: Added obsolete type detection when XAML elements are created

### Before
```
XamlC warning XC0618: Property, Property setter or BindableProperty "MyProperty" is deprecated.
```

### After
```
XamlC warning XC0618: "MyProperty" is deprecated: Use NewProperty instead.
XamlC error XC0619: "MyProperty" is obsolete: This property will be removed in the next version.
```

## Testing

- Added `Maui23961.xaml` / `.cs` - tests for warnings with `error: false`
- Added `Maui23961Error.rt.xaml` / `.cs` - tests for errors with `error: true`
- All 1780+ existing Xaml.UnitTests pass
- Samples build successfully

author: ellistarn
body:
## Summary

Migrate from `hack/toolchain.sh` to Go 1.24+ native `go tool` directive for managing developer tools.

## Prompts

This PR was generated using Amazon Q CLI with the following prompts:

| Prompt | Resolution |
|--------|------------|
| I want to migrate Karpenter to use Golang's latest support for go tool and get rid of our toolchain.sh script. | Added `tool` block to go.mod, updated Makefile and go:generate directives to use `go tool` |
| Can't we use go tool as part of any go generate commands embedded in the codebase? | Updated 8 files with `//go:generate` to use `go tool controller-gen` |
| Any thoughts on how we can collapse down those last two stragglers? | Consolidated remaining tool references in Makefile |
| I noticed you changed the controller-gen version which changed the formatting of the files. Was this necessary? | Reverted to original controller-gen version to avoid formatting churn |
| ok can you commit these changes with a summary of the changes, and use the gh cli to make a PR | Created PR with detailed description |
| I don't love that we have a custom binary floating in the home directory. Is there a more idiomatic way to do this? | Switched to standalone `golangci-lint-kube-api-linter` via `go tool` |
| Yeah can it run standalone? | Confirmed and implemented standalone usage |
| woah you can't just blow away .custom-gcl.yml | Explained why it's no longer needed |
| oh nevermind, I understand why we don't need it now. Let's rip it out. | Removed `.custom-gcl.yml` |
| So with the new approach to KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS, you can no longer run go test on specific files anymore. How do we address this? | Envtest auto-discovers from default location, removed KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS export |
| help me fix my go mod problem let's start with go mod tidy | Identified checksum mismatch with `go-control-plane/envoy` |
| can you debug the github actions that are failing | Fixed install-deps action to use `go tool setup-envtest`, added replace directive for envoy checksum issue |

## Changes

### go.mod
- Added `tool` block with all developer tools: `controller-gen`, `govulncheck`, `ginkgo`, `helm-docs`, `actionlint`, `go-licenses`, `ko`, `goveralls`, `setup-envtest`, `golangci-lint-kube-api-linter`
- Added replace directive to resolve `cloud.google.com/go/compute/metadata` ambiguity from transitive dependencies
- Added replace directive for `go-control-plane/envoy` v1.32.3 → v1.32.4 to fix upstream checksum mismatch

### go:generate directives
Updated 8 files to use `go tool controller-gen` instead of bare `controller-gen`:
- `pkg/apis/apis.go`
- `pkg/cloudprovider/types.go`
- `pkg/scheduling/hostportusage.go`
- `pkg/scheduling/volumeusage.go`
- `pkg/scheduling/requirement.go`
- `pkg/controllers/state/statenode.go`
- `pkg/test/v1alpha1/testnodeclass.go`
- `kwok/apis/apis.go`

### Makefile
- Updated to use `go tool` for: `ginkgo`, `govulncheck`, `go-licenses`, `helm-docs`, `actionlint`, `golangci-lint-kube-api-linter`
- Removed `toolchain` target (no longer needed)
- Removed `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS` export (envtest auto-discovers from default location)

### .github/actions/install-deps/action.yaml
- Removed toolchain cache and `make toolchain` call
- Now only caches envtest binaries and uses `go tool setup-envtest` directly
- Tools are now cached as part of Go's module cache (managed by `actions/setup-go`)

### Deleted
- `hack/toolchain.sh` - no longer needed
- `.custom-gcl.yml` - using standalone `golangci-lint-kube-api-linter` binary via `go tool` instead

## Benefits

- **Reproducible builds**: Tool versions are pinned in `go.mod`
- **No global installation**: Tools are managed per-module
- **Simpler setup**: Just `go mod download` then `go tool setup-envtest use 1.34.x` to download test assets
- **No custom binaries**: Everything runs via `go tool`, no binaries floating around
- **Direct test execution**: `go test ./pkg/...` works directly without setting environment variables
- **Native Go tooling**: Uses Go 1.24+ built-in feature

## Caching Strategy

The caching approach changes with this PR:
- **Before**: Separate toolchain cache (`~/go/bin`) keyed on `hack/toolchain.sh` hash
- **After**: Tools are part of Go's module cache (managed by `actions/setup-go`), only envtest binaries are cached separately

First CI run after merge will be slower as tools are downloaded fresh, but subsequent runs benefit from the module cache.

This commit does two things:

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR implements the "Multi-Label Semantic Clustering" feature using a global context strategy.

Key changes:
1.  **Global Taxonomy Agent**: A new `pydantic-ai` agent (`src/egregora/agents/taxonomy.py`) that accepts a list of cluster summaries and returns a comprehensive taxonomy map. This enables the LLM to contrast clusters against each other and produce distinct tags.
2.  **Clustering Operation**: `src/egregora/ops/taxonomy.py` orchestrates the process:
    *   Retrieves document vectors from the RAG backend.
    *   Performs K-Means clustering (using a dynamic $k$ heuristic).
    *   Aggregates "exemplar" posts (top 5 per cluster) into a single global prompt.
    *   Calls the agent once to generate the full taxonomy.
    *   Applies the generated tags to all documents in each cluster idempotently.
3.  **RAG Backend Extension**: Added `get_all_post_vectors` to `LanceDBRAGBackend` to support the clustering step by providing document centroids.
4.  **Pipeline Integration**: The feature is integrated into the `write` pipeline as a post-processing step, enabled when RAG is active.

This approach ensures higher quality tags by leveraging the LLM's ability to see the "forest" (all topics) rather than just the "trees" (individual clusters).

author: kiebor81
body:
Race condition in the final line:

```ruby
def synchronize_one(key, &block)
  return yield unless @sync
  @mutex.synchronize do
    @locks[key] ||= Mutex.new
  end
  @locks[key].synchronize(&block) 
end
```

Solved by holding the mutex reference while maintaining the global lock:

```ruby
def synchronize_one(key, &block)
  return yield unless @sync
  mtx = @mutex.synchronize do
    @locks[key] ||= Mutex.new
  end
  mtx.synchronize(&block)
end
```

Tests added:
- `test_remove_all_concurrent_with_get`
- `test_no_method_error_on_concurrent_remove_all`
- `test_synchronize_one_returns_working_mutex`

---

Only clearing `@hash` leaves `@locks` with orphaned mutexes. This results in unbound memory growth over time.

```ruby
def remove_all
  synchronize_all { @hash = {} }
end
```

Solved by:

```ruby
def remove_all
  synchronize_all do
    @hash = {}
    @locks = {}
  end
end
```

`test_locks_cleaned_up_after_remove_all` test added to confirm.

---

Similar to previous, removing key from `@hash` but left mutex in `@locks` causes memory leak.

```ruby
def remove(key)
  synchronize_one(key) { @hash.delete(key) { yield if block_given? } }
end
```

Solved by

```ruby
def remove(key)
  result = synchronize_one(key) { @hash.delete(key) { yield if block_given? } }
  synchronize_all { @locks.delete(key) }
  result
end
```

With test `test_locks_cleaned_up_after_remove`

---

Locks are not removed with deleted keys. This causes memory growth over time.

```ruby
def remove_by
  synchronize_all do
    count = 0
    @hash.each_key do |k|
      if yield(k)
        @hash.delete(k)
        count += 1
      end
    end
    count
  end
end
```

Solved by:

```ruby
def remove_by
  synchronize_all do
    count = 0
    @hash.each_key do |k|
      if yield(k)
        @hash.delete(k)
        @locks.delete(k)  # Clean up lock
        count += 1
      end
    end
    count
  end
end
```

Test added: `test_locks_cleaned_up_after_remove_by`

---

Expired key locks are not cleaned up.

```ruby
def clean
  synchronize_all do
    size_before = @hash.size
    @hash.delete_if { |key, _value| expired_unsafe?(key) }
    size_before - @hash.size
  end
end
```

Fixed:

```ruby
def clean
  synchronize_all do
    size_before = @hash.size
    @hash.delete_if do |key, _value|
      expired = expired_unsafe?(key)
      @locks.delete(key) if expired
      expired
    end
    size_before - @hash.size
  end
end
```

`test_locks_cleaned_up_after_clean` added for testing

---

No nil guard on dirty reads and race condition with unsynchronised locks

```ruby
if (dirty || @dirty) && locked?(key)
  synchronize_all do
    return @hash[key][:value] if expired_unsafe?(key) && @hash.key?(key)
  end
end
```

Fixed as

```ruby
if (dirty || @dirty) && locked?(key)
  synchronize_all do
    rec = @hash[key]
    return rec[:value] if !rec.nil? && expired_unsafe?(key)
  end
end
```

test added, `test_dirty_mode_nil_safety`

---

No error handling on background thread could cause collapse or recursive error

```ruby
Thread.new do
  synchronize_one(key) { calc(key, lifetime, &block) }
end
```

Fixed with failover to resynch with purge

```ruby
Thread.new do
  begin
    synchronize_one(key) { calc(key, lifetime, &block) }
  rescue StandardError => e
    synchronize_all do
      @hash.delete(key)
      @locks.delete(key)
    end
    raise e
  end
end
```

`test_eager_mode_with_error_in_block` added for testing. Prints intentional (RuntimeError) message in test output.

---

Corrected rake test task to match the public API and added line to remove plugins when developer is using Windows to avoid false test failure and bail outs.

---

After fixing rubocop violations, I noticed `Zache.get` was beyond the limit. Was initially going to add to exclusions, but because the function already had clear boundaries, was easy enough to split out and refactor.

body:
This PR allows us to add PDF attachments and revises the attachment logic in general.

It addresses part of https://github.com/GSA-TTS/pic-blm-cxworks/issues/346, bullet 14. Related to https://github.com/GSA-TTS/pic-blm-cxworks/pull/343.

## Notes:

The basic approach (thanks to @btylerburton and @mogul) is to merge PDFs. We do the following:
1. Extract our base html styles and use them in the two new templates below.
2. Create a simple template for an "attachment cover sheet" preceding each attachment. (This is mostly done because it is easier than adding a header to an existing PDF.)
3. Create a simple template for an image embedded into html.
4. In our artifact generation logic, we create one "base" PDF for all the non-attachment data, then render each attachment as a cover page (via the template in 2) + attachment-as-PDF. (For image attachments, we use the template from 3 and inject into a PDF to maintain styling. For PDF attachments ... we're done.)
5. We merge the base PDF with all of the attachment PDFs.
